meta.spec_reference: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2022 (ISO base media file format, 7th edition); ISO/IEC 14496-14:2003 (MP4 file format); ISO/IEC 14496-15:2014 (carriage of NAL unit structured video: avcC/hvcC and SampleEntry layout); ISO/IEC 14496-3:2009 subclause 1.6.2.1 and 4.4.1 (AudioSpecificConfig, esds); ISO/IEC 23001-7:2016 Common Encryption (tenc/senc/saiz/saio/pssh/sinf/schm/frma); Apple QuickTime File Format Specification (QTFF, rev. 2010-04-15) for the QuickTime-only atoms and the language / graphics-mode / matrix / opcolor tables the template cites at lines 37 and 151.

schema_extensions.name: synthetic box-payload keys
schema_extensions.why: The template routes mdat, every stsd sample-entry type (avc1/mp4a/avcC/esds and friends) and free/skip through its 'default: FSkip(contentsize)' branch at line 799, so those bytes exist in the file but have no declared field name to key on. They carry the highest-value constraint in this format - media samples must be a real elementary stream and sample entries must carry a real codec config - so a key is required. The bracket names the box type the bytes belong to and points at the default branch of the switch on hdr.type.value.

schema_extensions.name: bit_definitions
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries of type bitmask_constraint (mp4box.flag, mp4box.first_sample_flags, mp4box.sample_flags, mp4box.default_sample_flags, str_sidx.reference_size31_type1, mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block)
schema_extensions.why: MP4 packs structure-selecting switches into 24-bit FullBox flag words and 32-bit sample-flag words. A bare valid_bits integer cannot tell the rewrite step which bit turns on which following member, and getting that wrong makes the box unreadable, so each bit is named with its meaning and the boxes it applies to.

schema_extensions.name: per_box
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries whose .bt identifier is reused by several branches of the switch on hdr.type.value (mp4box.version, mp4box.flag, mp4box.flags, mp4box.entry_count, mp4box.sample_count, mp4box.entry, mp4box.entries, mp4box.reserved, mp4box.reserved2, mp4box.chunk_offset, mp4box.offset, mp4box.aux_info_type, mp4box.sample_size, mp4box.time_scale, mp4box.duration, mp4box.trackID, mp4box.matrix_structure, mp4box.create_time, mp4box.modify_time)
schema_extensions.why: The .bt declares these as separate members of different case branches but they all share one spelling, so a single key of the form STRUCT.field must carry the per-box-type detail or the constraint is ambiguous. per_box maps box type to the specific rule for that box.

schema_extensions.name: same_as
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries whose field is an instance of a small wrapper struct that already has its own authoritative entry (mp4box.language -> mp4lang.value; mp4box.create_time and mp4box.modify_time -> mp4time.value; mp4box.opcolor -> qtopcolor.red/green/blue; mp4box.balance, mp4box.volume, mp4box.preferred_volume -> fp16.value; mp4box.width, mp4box.height, mp4box.preferred_rate -> fp32.value)
schema_extensions.why: Duplicating a 106-value enumeration or a fixed-point rule under several keys invites divergence between copies; same_as points at the single authoritative entry while still giving the reader the local field type and evidence line.

schema_extensions.name: file_id_bytes
schema_extensions.why: The 010 template's '// ID Bytes:' header line (line 10) is the only place in the .bt where the file-level signature is stated, and it is expressed as byte-offset/value pairs rather than as a field comparison, so it needs its own home.

schema_extensions.name: array_length_is_free
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries of type calculated_value whose field is a count or an array bound
schema_extensions.why: Records explicitly that the NUMBER of elements is a free choice of the generator (a diversity axis, also listed in diversity_axes) and that the Tier A obligation is only that the number WRITTEN equals the number EMITTED. Without this flag a downstream reader could mistake the calculated_value tier for a cap on the count, which is precisely the GIF failure mode this task warns about.

schema_extensions.name: decoder_gate
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries where the field decides whether a real decoder proceeds (97 entries)
schema_extensions.why: Coverage, not validity, is the objective. decoder_gate states concretely what a real demuxer does with the field - whether it aborts, warns, clamps or ignores it - so the rewrite step can spend constraint effort where the decoder actually branches and leave the rest free.

schema_extensions.name: completeness_reason
schema_extensions.where: the 9 constraints entries of type enumerated_values whose completeness is 'partial'
schema_extensions.why: The prompt asks for completeness 'exhaustive' or 'partial' plus, if partial, why. Rather than fold the reason into the completeness string, it is carried in this separate key so completeness stays machine-comparable. The reason in every case is that the value space is open-ended - compatible brands, codec FourCCs, DRM system UUIDs, handler types - and that a listed subset must not be read as a cap on a free field.

schema_extensions.name: preferred_value
schema_extensions.where: 32 constraints entries of tier A or B, of types enumerated_values, bitmask_constraint and pattern_constraint; never on a tier C entry
schema_extensions.why: The prompt defines preferred_value only inside the enumerated_values type, so carrying it on bitmask_constraint and pattern_constraint entries is an extension. It names the value that reaches the most decoder code for that field, that is, the default a real muxer would write. It is a suggestion for the common case and never a narrowing: every entry that carries it also carries its full valid_values, valid_bits or pattern, and no tier C field carries it at all, because a preferred value on a free field would read as a cap.

schema_extensions.name: alternative_pattern
schema_extensions.why: A second acceptable byte pattern for one field where the specification permits either an all-zero test key or a real UUID; a single pattern key could not express the choice.

schema_extensions.name: template_compared_literals
schema_extensions.why: Lists exactly the FourCC string literals the .bt switch compares against, separately from the wider set the format allows. This distinguishes 'the template parses this box' from 'the format permits this box', which decides whether an unknown type reaches the default FSkip branch.

schema_extensions.name: payload_type, codec_or_standard and layout_derives_from
schema_extensions.where: the five constraints entries of type payload_wellformedness
schema_extensions.why: codec, must_produce, decoder_gate, generation_strategy, derives_from and content_is_free are all prompt-defined and are used as specified. These three are additions: payload_type gives a one-word classification of the byte region (elementary_stream, nested_box_sequence, encoded_codec_config, encoded_structured_metadata, unstructured_padding) so tooling can tell the load-bearing payloads from the free ones without parsing prose; codec_or_standard names the governing document rather than the codec, which matters for the two payloads that are not a codec at all (the DRM blob and the padding); layout_derives_from lists the declared fields that fix the payload's framing as distinct from its content, which derives_from alone does not separate.

schema_extensions.name: bit_layout, bit_meanings
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries of type bitmask_constraint (7 and 4 entries respectively)
schema_extensions.why: bit_layout gives the bit positions in the order the .bt reads them, which is not always the order the specification lists them; bit_meanings expands bit_definitions with the following members each bit causes to exist. Both exist because a bare valid_bits integer cannot tell the rewrite step which bit gates which field.

schema_extensions.name: offset_from
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries whose value is an offset (5 entries: mp4box.data_offset, mp4box.base_data_offset, mp4box.offset, mp4box.chunk_offset, mp4box.first_offset)
schema_extensions.why: States the anchor the offset is measured from, which differs per field: start of file, start of the enclosing moof, or start of mdat. Without it the rewrite step cannot compute the value, and an offset anchored wrongly is the single most common way an MP4 generator produces an unparseable file.

schema_extensions.name: must_remain_unconstrained and interacts_with inside constraints
schema_extensions.where: the three synthetic box-payload constraints entries (3 and 2 entries respectively)
schema_extensions.why: Repeats the diversity_axes instruction on the constraint entry itself, so that a reader of the payload entry - which is where a size-conscious author is most tempted to pin a dimension - sees the derive-the-payload rule in place.

schema_extensions.name: condition and the extra when/then keys in dependencies
schema_extensions.where: the dependencies array; condition on 9 of the 64 entries
schema_extensions.why: condition scopes a dependency to the files it applies to, for example only when moov contains mvex, or only when the template skips the box in question. The extra keys inside when and then (tier, type, required, equals, covers, includes_self, algorithm) carry the derivation detail of the dependent field so each dependency is self-contained and needs no lookup back into constraints.

schema_extensions.name: tier_policy in meta
schema_extensions.why: tier_counts is prompt-defined and used as specified. tier_policy is an addition: it states the test applied to assign each tier, records the single Tier C entry whose type is payload_wellformedness rather than unconstrained and why valid_range does not apply to a byte array, and records the depth-over-size decision that makes the encoded payloads Tier A even though emitting a real elementary stream costs far more output than emitting random bytes.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_value_scan in meta
schema_extensions.why: The completeness checklist requires a specific re-scan for magic numbers, signatures, section markers, block terminators and field separators as Tier A fixed_value entries. This format has none, so the re-scan result and the reasoning for every near-miss candidate are recorded here rather than left as a silent absence, which a reader could not distinguish from an oversight.

meta.structure_note: An MP4/MOV file is a flat, big-endian sequence of boxes (QuickTime atoms) that recursively contain further boxes, each prefixed by a 4-byte size and a 4-byte type FourCC, plus a 64-bit largesize when size==1; the format has no whole-file magic number (its signature is the FourCC at byte offset 4 of the first box), no CRC or checksum of any kind, and no compressed container framing, so the only encoded-stream payloads are the elementary-stream media samples inside mdat and the codec configuration records (avcC/hvcC/esds) inside stsd sample entries, both of which this template skips blindly through its default FSkip() branch.
meta.fixed_value_scan: Checklist item 1 re-scan result: this format has no fixed_value field, and the absence is a property of MP4 rather than an omission. MP4 carries no whole-file magic number (the 010 signature at .bt line 10 is the FourCC at byte offset 4, which is the field boxheader.type, recorded as Tier A enumerated_values with the 'ftyp first' rule in dependencies), no CRC or Adler checksum of any kind, no block terminator and no field separator: boxes are framed entirely by boxheader.size, which is Tier A calculated_value, and every array is framed by its own count field, also Tier A calculated_value. The spec-mandated-zero fields were considered for fixed_value and deliberately left Tier C: tenc reserved1 (line 505) and reserved2 (line 506), sidx reserved (line 640), mvhd reserved[10] (line 759), smhd reserved (line 773), tkhd reserved (line 781), reserved2 (line 783) and reserved3 (line 787). No decoder branch reads them - ffmpeg's mov_read_default and mov_read_trak ignore them outright - so by the tier test in meta.tier_policy they are free, and each entry's notes records that conforming files emit 0 so a conformance-minded reader is not misled. Their byte widths are fixed by the declarations and are not free; only the byte values are.

tier_policy.A: Structurally load-bearing: a wrong value makes the file unparseable or makes a real demuxer reject it outright. Box sizes and types, the version/flag words that select which members follow, every count that sizes an array, and the encoded payloads whose absence yields zero decoded streams (mdat samples, stsd sample entries, pssh Data). Constrained to the exact legal value, set or derivation.
tier_policy.B: Semantically load-bearing but not parse-breaking: a wrong value still yields a file a demuxer opens, yet it silently disables a decoder path (a brand that turns off the fragmented or CENC branch, a handler_type that turns off the video or audio path, a timescale that makes every timestamp wrong, a scheme_type that turns off the CENC reader). Constrained to the enumerated or pattern set that keeps the path reachable, with the full set given rather than a single preferred value.
tier_policy.C: Free: no decoder branch depends on the value. Reserved fields, padding, creation and modification times, matrix and colour-metadata fields the parser only reports, and the content of any box the template skips. Left at the full width of the declared integer type with no span narrowing, and every one of them is listed again in diversity_axes with must_remain_unconstrained true.
tier_policy.payload_exception: Exactly one Tier C entry, mp4box[type="free"].content, carries type payload_wellformedness rather than unconstrained. It is a byte array rather than an integer field, so valid_range does not apply; its freedom is expressed by content_is_free true, must_produce 'Nothing', and codec 'none'. The four other payload_wellformedness entries are Tier A because their bytes are load-bearing to a decoder even though this template skips them.
tier_policy.depth_over_size: Where covering a field deeply costs output bytes, depth wins: the encoded payloads are Tier A even though emitting a real elementary stream is far more expensive than emitting random bytes. Where covering a field costs nothing but bytes, the bytes are left free and bounded only by the output_budget mechanism in structure, never by a repeat count or an integer span.

fp16.value.tier_rationale: An 8.8 fixed-point scalar (preferred_volume, smhd balance, tkhd volume) that no MP4 or QuickTime decoder validates; pinning it would remove free variation in the movie and track headers without buying a single extra decoded line.
fp16.value.description: Signed 8.8 fixed-point value; the raw int16 is interpreted as value/256 and any bit pattern is legal.
fp16.value.notes: Read by ReadFP16 (line 175) purely for display. BigEndian() at line 20 applies to the whole file. Real-world files usually carry 0x0100 (1.0) for volume and 0 for balance, but nothing checks either.

fp32.value.tier_rationale: A 16.16 fixed-point scalar carrying tkhd track width, tkhd track height and mvhd preferred_rate - exactly the class of dimension field the task forbids narrowing; a decoder reads it and moves on regardless of magnitude.
fp32.value.description: Signed 16.16 fixed-point value interpreted as value/65536; used for the tkhd display dimensions and the mvhd preferred rate. Any int32 bit pattern is legal.
fp32.value.notes: tkhd width/height are DISPLAY dimensions in 16.16 pixels and are independent of the coded dimensions the codec takes from its own config record (the SPS for H.264, the AudioSpecificConfig for AAC), so they can be varied across the whole int32 span without invalidating any payload.

fp32uvw.value.tier_rationale: The 2.30 translation components of the transform matrix; decoders apply the matrix arithmetically and never reject a value, so constraining it would only reduce diversity.
fp32uvw.value.description: Signed 2.30 fixed-point value used for the u/v/w translation column of the mvhd and tkhd matrix; interpreted as value/1073741824.
fp32uvw.value.notes: QTFF specifies the identity matrix as 0x00010000,0,0,0,0x00010000,0,0,0,0x40000000; a non-identity or degenerate matrix is still parsed and applied.

matrix.a.tier_rationale: A transformation-matrix coefficient: a wrong value rotates, scales or mirrors the picture but no decoder refuses the file, so pinning it to the identity value would delete free variation from every mvhd and tkhd that carries a matrix.
matrix.a.description: Horizontal-scale coefficient (row 1, column 1) of the 3x3 track or movie transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value.
matrix.a.notes: The identity matrix is a=0x00010000, b=0, u=0, c=0, d=0x00010000, v=0, x=0, y=0, w=0x40000000. QTFF recommends it but nothing in the parser or a conforming decoder enforces it, and rotation matrices (90/180/270 degrees) are the common real-world deviation.

matrix.b.tier_rationale: A transformation-matrix coefficient with no decoder-enforced value; see matrix.a.
matrix.b.description: Vertical-shear coefficient (row 1, column 2) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value.
matrix.b.notes: Non-zero b is exactly how a 90-degree rotation is encoded, so it must stay free.

matrix.u.tier_rationale: The homogeneous row of a transformation matrix is never validated by a demuxer; a wrong value at worst makes the perspective term odd, which no decoder checks.
matrix.u.description: Horizontal homogeneous coefficient (row 1, column 3) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 2.30 fixed-point value.
matrix.u.notes: Always 0 in practice; the 2.30 encoding differs from the 16.16 encoding of the a/b/c/d coefficients, which is why the .bt uses a distinct typedef.

matrix.c.tier_rationale: A transformation-matrix coefficient with no decoder-enforced value; see matrix.a.
matrix.c.description: Horizontal-shear coefficient (row 2, column 1) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value.
matrix.c.notes: Non-zero c is how a 270-degree rotation is encoded.

matrix.d.tier_rationale: A transformation-matrix coefficient with no decoder-enforced value; see matrix.a.
matrix.d.description: Vertical-scale coefficient (row 2, column 2) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value.
matrix.d.notes: A negative d flips the picture vertically; nothing refuses that.

matrix.v.tier_rationale: The homogeneous row of a transformation matrix is never validated by a demuxer; see matrix.u.
matrix.v.description: Vertical homogeneous coefficient (row 2, column 3) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 2.30 fixed-point value.

matrix.x.tier_rationale: A translation term of a transformation matrix; a wrong value shifts the picture but no decoder refuses the file, so it is free.
matrix.x.description: Horizontal translation coefficient (row 3, column 1) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value.
matrix.x.notes: Used to offset a rotated track back into the visible frame.

matrix.y.tier_rationale: A translation term of a transformation matrix; see matrix.x.
matrix.y.description: Vertical translation coefficient (row 3, column 2) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value.
matrix.y.notes: Used to offset a rotated track back into the visible frame.

matrix.w.tier_rationale: The homogeneous scale term of a transformation matrix is never validated by a demuxer; see matrix.u.
matrix.w.description: Homogeneous scale coefficient (row 3, column 3) of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 2.30 fixed-point value.
matrix.w.notes: 0x40000000 (1.0 in 2.30) is the conventional identity value; a different value still parses.

fourcc.value.tier_rationale: This is the 4-byte section marker of every box, brand and handler in the file: the template switches on it (line 469) and a real demuxer dispatches on it, so a value outside the registered FourCC alphabet makes the box be skipped or the file be refused before any useful work happens.
fourcc.value.description: Four characters forming a registered ISO BMFF or QuickTime code; used for box types, brand codes and handler types.
fourcc.value.pattern: exactly 4 octets, each drawn from the printable registered-FourCC alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, space, and the punctuation used by registered codes: '-', '.', '+', '*', '/' and the QuickTime 0xA9 copyright byte); never NUL, never a control byte, never random binary
fourcc.value.decoder_gate: An unregistered or non-printable FourCC forces the demuxer down its unknown-box path: this template executes 'default: FSkip(contentsize)' at line 799 and ffmpeg logs 'unknown atom' and skips the payload, so the box contents are never interpreted and no track is built from them.
fourcc.value.notes: The concrete legal value sets live on the fields that instantiate this type: boxheader.type (box type registry), compatible_brand.brand and mp4box.major_brand (brand registry), mp4box.type and mp4box.subtype (hdlr component and handler types). This entry states the byte-level rule they all share.

boxheader.size.tier_rationale: This is the front gate of the whole format: every box boundary, the child-box loop at line 486 and every contentsize computation at line 167 are derived from it, so a value that disagrees with the bytes written makes the parser lose frame and the demuxer reject the file.
boxheader.size.description: Total size of the box in bytes, counting the 8-byte header itself (16 when size==1) plus all content and all child boxes.
boxheader.size.algorithm: byte count of the whole box: size = sizeof(boxheader) + number_of_content_and_child_bytes_actually_written
boxheader.size.covers: the entire box: this field itself, boxheader.type, boxheader.size64 when present, and every content field and child mp4box up to endOffset
boxheader.size.decoder_gate: If size is smaller than what the box holds, the parser reinterprets leftover content bytes as the next box header and desynchronises for the rest of the file; if larger, it runs off the end and the demuxer fails with invalid data. Either way nothing after the first bad box is parsed.
boxheader.size.notes: Computed by BoxSize() at line 170 and ContentSize() at line 165: ContentSize = (size64 if present else size) - sizeof(boxheader); endOffset = startOffset + BoxSize(hdr) at line 466. Minimum legal value is 8 (16 when size==1). ISO BMFF also permits size==0 meaning 'extends to end of file', but ContentSize() would then underflow to a huge uint64 and the template would run to EOF, so size==0 must NOT be emitted. size is never pinned to a constant: it is derived from the bytes actually written, which is what lets every box vary in length.

boxheader.type.tier_rationale: The box-type FourCC is the section marker the entire parser dispatches on (switch at line 469); a value outside the registry makes the box be skipped by FSkip, and a real demuxer that finds no recognised boxes builds no tracks and exits after the probe.
boxheader.type.description: Four-character box type selecting which content layout follows; must be a registered ISO BMFF or QuickTime box type for the box to be interpreted at all.
boxheader.type.file_id_bytes: line 10 states '//  ID Bytes: [+4] 66 74 79 70, [+4] 6D 6F 6F 76, [+4] 6D 64 61 74' - the 010 file signature is the FourCC at byte offset 4 being 'ftyp' (66 74 79 70), 'moov' (6D 6F 6F 76) or 'mdat' (6D 64 61 74). A generated file that does not carry one of these at offset 4 is not recognised as MP4 at all, so the first top-level box must be 'ftyp' and offset 4 must read 66 74 79 70.
boxheader.type.completeness_reason: The ISO BMFF and QuickTime FourCC registries are open-ended - any registered code is legal and every new codec adds sample-entry types - so an exhaustive list is impossible. valid_values above is the union of every type this template names (all cases of the BoxComment switch at lines 205-243 and all cases of the parsing switch at lines 469-798, including 'tfhd', 'sinf', 'schi', 'frma', 'tenc', 'schm', 'enca' and 'smhd' which appear only in the parsing switch, and 'dref' which appears only in BoxComment) plus the common spec-registered types a real demuxer branches on.
boxheader.type.decoder_gate: The demuxer builds its track list by walking recognised box types; unrecognised ones are skipped. A file whose top-level types are all unknown yields zero tracks and the decoder exits immediately after the probe.
boxheader.type.notes: Every value in valid_values must stay emittable - the unknown/skip branch at line 799, the container branch at line 486 and each codec-specific sample-entry branch are distinct code paths worth covering. Do not narrow this list to the ones that parse deepest.

boxheader.size64.tier_rationale: When size==1 the parser takes every box boundary from this 64-bit largesize; a value that disagrees with the bytes actually written desynchronises the remainder of the file exactly as a bad 32-bit size does.
boxheader.size64.description: 64-bit total box size in bytes, present only when boxheader.size == 1; includes the 16-byte extended header itself.
boxheader.size64.algorithm: byte count of the whole box: size64 = 16 + number_of_content_and_child_bytes_actually_written
boxheader.size64.covers: the entire box: the 8-byte size/type header, this field itself, and every content field and child mp4box up to endOffset
boxheader.size64.decoder_gate: A largesize that does not match the written bytes makes the next box header be read from the wrong offset; the demuxer then reports an invalid box and stops parsing the file.
boxheader.size64.notes: Conditional on size==1 (line 374: 'if (size == 1)'). Minimum legal value is 16. sizeof(boxheader) evaluates to 16 in this case, so ContentSize() = size64 - 16. The number of bytes in the box is free; only the written value must match it.

compatible_brand.brand.tier_rationale: A wrong brand does not make a conforming decoder refuse the file - it is a compatibility hint collected into a list - so it fails the Tier A test, but the legal set is a finite registry of FourCC codes, so it is Tier B and every registered brand must stay emittable.
compatible_brand.brand.description: Four-character brand code in the ftyp compatible_brands list declaring which specification versions this file conforms to.
compatible_brand.brand.completeness_reason: Brand codes are an open registry maintained in the ISO BMFF registered brand list; any registered FourCC is legal and vendors add new ones, so no exhaustive enumeration exists. The set above covers every brand the mainstream decoders recognise.
compatible_brand.brand.decoder_gate: A decoder that does not recognise the major_brand may still accept the file when a compatible brand it supports is listed; an entirely unknown brand set makes strict readers fall back to generic ISO BMFF handling, which is a different and shallower path but not a rejection.
compatible_brand.brand.notes: The ftyp compatible_brands list is variable length: the template loops 'while (FTell() < startof(major_brand) + contentsize)' at line 724, so the number of compatible_brand entries is whatever fits in the box. That count is free - see the ftyp output_budget in structure.

mp4time.value.tier_rationale: Creation and modification timestamps are explicitly Tier C: no decoder validates them, and pinning them would strip free variation from mvhd, mdhd and tkhd without changing a single parse path.
mp4time.value.description: Seconds since the classic Mac OS epoch (midnight 1 January 1904), stored as uint32 (uint64 when the enclosing box version is 1); any value is legal.
mp4time.value.notes: ReadTime (line 265) subtracts the constant 2082844800 (line 270) purely for display; the parser never validates the result. Values below that constant simply render as pre-1970 dates.

mp4lang.value.tier_rationale: A wrong language code does not make a conforming decoder refuse the file - ReadLang (line 274) merely renders it - so it fails the Tier A test, but its legal set is a finite published table, so it is Tier B and every code must stay emittable.
mp4lang.value.description: 16-bit language field of mdhd: either a classic Macintosh language code from the QuickTime table, or an ISO-639-2/T three-letter code packed into three 5-bit groups.
mp4lang.value.completeness_reason: The 106 codes above are the exhaustive QuickTime Macintosh language table as declared by the enum qtlang at lines 38-149 (value 86 is not assigned by the table, and 28, 29 and 87 each carry two spellings: qtlLettish/qtlLatvian, qtlSaami/qtlSami, qtlGalla/qtlOromo). The list is nonetheless only partial for the FIELD, because ISO BMFF also permits the packed ISO-639-2/T form described in alternative_pattern, which is a distinct legal encoding rather than a member of the enum.
mp4lang.value.alternative_pattern: values >= 0x0400 and != 32767 encode an ISO-639-2/T three-letter code as three 5-bit groups: iso[0] = ((value & 0x7c00) >> 10) + 0x60, iso[1] = ((value & 0x03e0) >> 5) + 0x60, iso[2] = (value & 0x001f) + 0x60 (lines 282-284). Any value whose three 5-bit groups each fall in 1..26 is therefore legal; e.g. 0x55C4 decodes to 'und' and 0x12C5 to 'eng'. The most significant bit of the 16-bit field must be 0.

template_compared_literals.meaning: ReadLang switches between the Macintosh table (value < 0x0400, or the explicit qtlUnspecified sentinel) and the packed ISO-639-2 form; 0x0400 is the boundary literal the template compares against.

mp4lang.value.notes: preferred_value names 32767 (qtlUnspecified), 0 (qtlEnglish), 21956 = 0x55C4 (packed ISO-639-2 'und') and 5575 = 0x15C7 (packed ISO-639-2 'eng'); these exercise both branches of ReadLang. All 106 enum values plus every packed ISO-639-2 value must remain emittable.

qtopcolor.red.tier_rationale: A colour value: no decoder validates it, and vmhd opcolor only affects how transparent pixels are composited, so pinning it would cost diversity for nothing.
qtopcolor.red.description: Red component of the vmhd operation colour, a 16-bit QuickTime colour channel; any value is legal.
qtopcolor.red.notes: ReadOpcolor (line 289) only formats the three channels for display. QTFF's default opcolor is 0x8000 for each of red, green and blue (mid-grey).

qtopcolor.green.tier_rationale: A colour value the decoder never validates; constraining it removes free variation from every video track header.
qtopcolor.green.description: Green component of the vmhd operation colour; any value is legal.

qtopcolor.blue.tier_rationale: A colour value the decoder never validates; constraining it removes free variation from every video track header.
qtopcolor.blue.description: Blue component of the vmhd operation colour; any value is legal.

elst_entry.duration.tier_rationale: A duration is explicitly Tier C; no decoder refuses a file because an edit segment is long, short or zero, and pinning durations would collapse the timeline diversity that drives the demuxer's seek and edit-list code.
elst_entry.duration.description: Duration of one edit-list segment in movie time-scale units; any uint32 is legal, including 0.

evidence.snippet: uint32 duration <name="Duration", comment="Duration of this edit segment in movie time scale units (specified in mvhd box)">;

elst_entry.duration.notes: An empty edit (media_time == 0xFFFFFFFF) is a legal and separately handled case in demuxers, so the full uint32 span including its endpoints is meaningful.

elst_entry.media_time.tier_rationale: A start timestamp; decoders branch on the empty-edit sentinel but never refuse a value, so it stays free.
elst_entry.media_time.description: Start time of the edit segment in media time-scale units; 0xFFFFFFFF (-1 as int32) marks an empty edit.

evidence.snippet: uint32 media_time <name="Media Time", comment="Start time of this edit segment in media time scale units (specified in mdhd box)">;

elst_entry.media_time.notes: Both the empty-edit sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF and ordinary values should be emitted - they take different paths through the demuxer's edit-list application.

elst_entry.media_rate.tier_rationale: A 16.16 playback rate that no decoder validates; constraining it costs diversity for no depth.
elst_entry.media_rate.description: Relative rate at which to play this edit segment, as an fp32 (16.16) value.

evidence.snippet: fp32 media_rate <name="Media Rate", comment="Relative rate at which to play this edit segment">;

elst_entry.media_rate.notes: Real files carry 0x00010000 (1.0). QTFF pairs this with a 16-bit media_rate_integer plus a 16-bit fraction; the template models it as one fp32.

tkhd_flags.dummy.tier_rationale: Reserved bytes that decoders mask off before testing any flag bit, so a wrong value still yields a fully processed file; pinning them to zero would delete free bytes.
tkhd_flags.dummy.description: The two high bytes of the 24-bit tkhd flags word; reserved by the spec but never validated.
tkhd_flags.dummy.notes: QTFF and ISO BMFF define only the low 4 bits of the 24-bit flags word; readers AND the word with 0xF, so these bytes cannot change behaviour.

tkhd_flags.dummy2.tier_rationale: The four reserved bits above the track flags; masked away by every decoder, so leaving them free costs nothing and adds diversity.
tkhd_flags.dummy2.description: Four reserved bits of the tkhd flags low byte, sitting above the four track flag bits.
tkhd_flags.dummy2.notes: Bit order in the template runs high-to-low within the byte: dummy2 occupies bits 7-4, then track_in_poster, track_in_preview, track_in_movie and track_enabled occupy bits 3-0.

tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.tier_rationale: A one-bit flag: a wrong value does not make the decoder refuse the file, but its legal set is exactly {0,1} and the two states select different presentation paths.
tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.description: Track is used in the movie poster (QuickTime track flag 0x08).
tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.notes: ReadTkhdFlags (line 305) tests all four bits independently, so each of the 16 combinations is a distinct path.

tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.tier_rationale: A one-bit flag with legal set {0,1}; a wrong value does not cause rejection, so it is Tier B, not A.
tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.description: Track is used in the movie preview (QuickTime track flag 0x04).

tkhd_flags.track_in_movie.tier_rationale: A one-bit flag with legal set {0,1}; nothing refuses the file if it is cleared, but it selects whether the track participates in playback, so both states must be emitted.
tkhd_flags.track_in_movie.description: Track is used in the movie (QuickTime track flag 0x02).
tkhd_flags.track_in_movie.notes: Some players only play tracks with this bit set, so 1 is preferred for reaching the media pipeline while 0 must still be emitted.

tkhd_flags.track_enabled.tier_rationale: A one-bit flag with legal set {0,1}; a disabled track is still parsed, so it fails the Tier A test, but clearing it in every file would delete the enabled-track path.
tkhd_flags.track_enabled.description: Track is enabled (QuickTime track flag 0x01); the bit every player tests before using a track.
tkhd_flags.track_enabled.notes: Emit 1 in most files so the track reaches the codec, and 0 in some files so the disabled-track branch is covered too.

vmhd_flags.dummy.tier_rationale: Reserved bytes in the vmhd flags word that decoders mask off; leaving them free adds entropy at zero depth cost.
vmhd_flags.dummy.description: The two high bytes of the 24-bit vmhd flags word; reserved.
vmhd_flags.dummy.notes: ISO BMFF requires vmhd flags to be 1 (no_lean_ahead set); the reserved bits are not checked by readers.

vmhd_flags.dummy2.tier_rationale: Seven reserved bits above the single defined vmhd flag; no reader tests them.
vmhd_flags.dummy2.description: Seven reserved bits of the vmhd flags low byte.
vmhd_flags.dummy2.notes: dummy2 occupies bits 7-1 of the byte; no_lean_ahead is bit 0.

vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.tier_rationale: A one-bit flag whose legal set is {0,1}; a wrong value never causes rejection, so it is Tier B rather than Tier A, but ISO BMFF fixes it to 1 so that value should dominate.
vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.description: Video media header 'no lean ahead' flag; ISO BMFF specifies that this bit shall be set to 1.
vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.notes: ReadVmhdFlags (line 327) only renders the bit. Emitting 0 in some files covers the spec-violating-but-accepted path.

str_stsc.first_chunk.tier_rationale: first_chunk defines where each stsc run starts; a run boundary outside the chunk table makes the resulting chunk-to-sample map invalid, which the demuxer detects while building the track rather than while decoding a frame.
str_stsc.first_chunk.description: 1-based index of the first chunk of this stsc run within the stco/co64 chunk table.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.6.1 (SampleToChunkBox): first_chunk is a 1-based chunk index into the chunk offset table and the entries must be in increasing order.

str_stsc.first_chunk.algorithm: index of the chunk at which this run's samples_per_chunk takes effect, counted from 1
str_stsc.first_chunk.covers: no bytes of its own; it is an index into the chunk_offset array of the sibling stco/co64 box

stsc: entry_count >= 1; a stsc with no entries leaves the chunk map undefined
1 <= entry[0].first_chunk <= chunk_count, where chunk_count is the entry_count of the sibling stco/co64
entry[i].first_chunk < entry[i+1].first_chunk for every consecutive pair

str_stsc.first_chunk.decoder_gate: The demuxer expands stsc into a per-chunk sample count and cross-checks it against the chunk table; a first_chunk outside that table leaves chunks with no sample count, so the track is rejected before any sample is read.
str_stsc.first_chunk.notes: The .bt declares this struct at line 427 and instantiates it only at line 685, 'str_stsc entry[entry_count];' inside case "stsc". The NUMBER of stsc entries is free; the Tier A obligation is only that the run boundaries written agree with the chunk table and the sample table.

str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.tier_rationale: stsc is not merely read: its sample counts define how every chunk maps to samples, and the demuxer validates the expanded table against stsz and stco before building a track, so a value that disagrees makes the track unusable.
str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.description: Number of samples in each chunk from first_chunk up to the next run's first_chunk minus one.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.6.1: samples_per_chunk is an integer greater than zero and the runs taken together must account for every sample in the track.

str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.algorithm: number of samples the demuxer reads out of each chunk covered by this run; must satisfy sum over all runs of (run_length * samples_per_chunk) == stsz sample_count, with the final run allowed to be partial
str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.covers: no bytes of its own; it sizes how many stsz sample sizes each chunk consumes

stsc: sum over runs of (run_length * samples_per_chunk) == stsz sample_count when stsz sample_size != 0
when stsz sample_size == 0 the last chunk may hold fewer than samples_per_chunk entries, so the sum may stop at or just below the length of the entry_size array

str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.decoder_gate: The chunk-to-sample map drives every stco seek; a samples_per_chunk that overruns or underruns the sample table makes the demuxer report a corrupt sample table and drop the track.
str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.notes: The .bt spelling is samples_per_chunk (plural). It is the value a careless reader would be tempted to fix at one sample per chunk, which would delete the multi-sample-chunk path.

str_stsc.sample_description_index.tier_rationale: This index selects which stsd sample entry describes the chunk's samples; an index of 0 or one beyond stsd entry_count names a codec configuration that does not exist, so the demuxer cannot instantiate a decoder for the track.
str_stsc.sample_description_index.description: 1-based index into the sibling stsd box's sample-entry array naming the codec that describes the samples of this run's chunks.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.6.1: sample_description_index is an integer greater than zero indexing the SampleEntry array of the SampleDescriptionBox.

str_stsc.sample_description_index.algorithm: 1-based index of the chosen mp4box entry inside the stsd entries[] array written at line 667
str_stsc.sample_description_index.covers: no bytes of its own; it points at one of the stsd sample entries

stsc: 1 <= sample_description_index <= stsd entry_count for every entry

str_stsc.sample_description_index.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stsc stores the index and mov_read_stsd must have populated that slot; an out-of-table index leaves the stream's codec context empty and mov_read_trak fails with 'could not find codec parameters', so no stream is exposed.
str_stsc.sample_description_index.notes: Real single-codec files use 1 throughout. Values above 1 are legal and exercise the multi-sample-entry path, so both must be emittable.

str_stts.sample_count.tier_rationale: The stts run lengths are summed by the demuxer to derive the track's total duration and sample count, which it then cross-checks against stsz and stsc; a sum that disagrees invalidates the track before any sample is decoded.
str_stts.sample_count.description: Number of consecutive samples sharing the following sample_delta in this stts run.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.6.1.1 (TimeToSampleBox): the run counts enumerate every sample of the track exactly once.

str_stts.sample_count.algorithm: sum of all entry[i].sample_count over the stts entry array == the sample_count written in the sibling stsz box
str_stts.sample_count.covers: no bytes of its own; it counts samples described by the sibling stsz/stsc tables

stts: entry_count >= 1 for a non-fragmented track, otherwise the track has no timeline
for a fragmented track stts may be absent entirely and the timeline is taken from trun sample_duration instead

str_stts.sample_count.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stts accumulates the counts into the track duration and sample count; when the accumulated count disagrees with stsz it warns about a broken sample table and truncates or drops the track, so the media pipeline is never entered.
str_stts.sample_count.notes: The .bt declares this struct at line 434 and instantiates it only at line 679, 'str_stts entry[entry_count];' inside case "stts". The number of runs is free.

str_stts.sample_delta.tier_rationale: A duration is explicitly Tier C: sample_delta sizes the timeline but nothing in the parser or a conforming demuxer validates its magnitude, and pinning it would remove the frame-rate and variable-frame-duration diversity that drives the demuxer's timestamp arithmetic.
str_stts.sample_delta.description: Delta in time-scale units between consecutive samples for this stts run; any uint32 is legal, including 0.
str_stts.sample_delta.notes: sample_delta == 0 is legal and produces a zero-length run that some demuxers special-case, so it must stay emittable. Large deltas are equally legal and drive different seek-arithmetic paths.

str_stsd.contentSize.tier_rationale: This is a byte count of the sample-description payload that follows it; if it disagrees with the bytes written, the parser reads the wrong number of content bytes and desynchronises, exactly like any other length field.
str_stsd.contentSize.description: Total byte length of one stsd sample description, including this 4-byte field itself.
str_stsd.contentSize.covers: this field plus the immediately following str_stsd.content array
str_stsd.contentSize.decoder_gate: The array is sized 'byte content[contentSize - 4]' at line 443, so a contentSize below 4 underflows the array bound and one larger than the bytes present runs off the end of the box.
str_stsd.contentSize.notes: str_stsd is declared at line 440 but is DEAD in this revision: its only instantiation, 'str_stsd description[entry_count];' at line 666, is commented out and replaced by 'mp4box entries[entry_count];' at line 667. It is recorded because the declaration is still in the .bt and a rewrite that re-enables it must keep the length honest. The authoritative live path for sample entries is mp4box.entries.

str_stsd.content.tier_rationale: These bytes are the sample-entry payload - the VisualSampleEntry or AudioSampleEntry header plus its codec configuration child boxes - which the demuxer parses to learn the codec, the geometry and the decoder config; random bytes here mean no codec is identified and no stream is created.
str_stsd.content.description: The opaque content run of one stsd sample description, holding a sample entry and its codec configuration boxes.

evidence.note: The commented-out loop at lines 444-448 shows the author's intent: these bytes are themselves a sequence of mp4box children, which is what the live path at line 667 does instead.

str_stsd.content.codec_or_standard: ISO/IEC 14496-15 (avcC, hvcC, vpcC, av1C); ISO/IEC 14496-14 (esds for mp4v); ISO/IEC 14496-3 subclause 1.6.2.1 (esds AudioSpecificConfig for mp4a); ETSI TS 102 366 (dac3, dec3); ALAC magic cookie; RFC 7845 (dOps)
str_stsd.content.codec: selected by the sample-entry FourCC in the box header that precedes these bytes: avc1/avc3 (H.264 with an avcC child), hvc1/hev1 (HEVC with an hvcC child), mp4v (MPEG-4 Visual with an esds child), mp4a (AAC with an esds child), ac-3/ec-3 (with dac3/dec3), alac, Opus (with dOps), vp08/vp09 (with vpcC), av01 (with av1C), tx3g/stpp/wvtt (timed text), enca/encv (CENC-encrypted forms of the above).
str_stsd.content.must_produce: A complete SampleEntry: 6 reserved bytes, a 2-byte data_reference_index, then the codec-specific fixed fields (for video: pre_defined and reserved uint16/uint32 trio, 8-byte pre_defined2, width and height as uint16, horizresolution and vertresolution both 0x00480000, 4 reserved bytes, frame_count 1, a 32-byte compressorname whose first byte is its length, depth 0x0018, int16 pre_defined -1; for audio: uint16 channelcount, uint16 samplesize, uint16 pre_defined, uint16 reserved, uint32 samplerate as 16.16), then the codec configuration child boxes each carrying a correct boxheader.size and boxheader.type.
str_stsd.content.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_default descends into stsd and calls mov_read_video_sample_entry or mov_read_audio_sample_entry; if the geometry, compressorname or child boxes are nonsense it logs a header decode error or finds no avcC/hvcC/esds and leaves the stream's codec_id as AV_CODEC_ID_NONE, so the track is never decoded.
str_stsd.content.generation_strategy: Do not emit these bytes blindly. Build the sample entry from the codec chosen for the track: write the 8-byte entry header (size, FourCC), the fixed fields above carrying the real width/height or channelcount/samplerate, then append the codec configuration box (avcC holding a real SPS and PPS, hvcC holding real VPS/SPS/PPS, esds holding a real AudioSpecificConfig) as a nested mp4box with its own correct size, and finally set the outer boxheader.size to the byte count of everything written. Derive the entry from the track's declared geometry and codec, never the reverse.
str_stsd.content.notes: Dead declaration in this revision - see str_stsd.contentSize. The live equivalent is the synthetic key mp4box[type="stsd"].sample_entry, which carries the same obligation for the path the template actually walks.

str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.tier_rationale: The low 31 bits are a byte size the demuxer adds up to walk the segment index; a value that does not equal the real byte length of the referenced subsegment makes the next reference point at the wrong offset, so the index cannot be followed and seeking fails.
str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.description: One sidx reference word packing a 1-bit reference_type in bit 31 and a 31-bit referenced_size in bits 30-0.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.16.3.3 (SegmentIndexBox) packs reference_type (1 bit) and referenced_size (31 bits) into one 32-bit word; the .bt names the field after that packing.

str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.bit_layout: bit 31 = reference_type: 0 means the reference points at a media segment (a moof+mdat pair), 1 means it points at another sidx index box. bits 30-0 = referenced_size: the total number of bytes of the referenced material, counted from the end of this sidx box, or from the end of the preceding reference for every later reference.
bit_meanings: 0x80000000 (2147483648) reference_type = index segment (points at a nested sidx)
0x00000000 (0) reference_type = media segment (points at a moof+mdat pair)
0x7FFFFFFF (2147483647) mask for referenced_size = byte length of the referenced material, a free count that must equal the bytes actually written
str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.completeness_reason: The word has exactly two documented subfields and no reserved bits; every one of the 32 bits is either the type flag or part of the size.

sidx: referenced_size (bits 30-0) of reference[i] == the byte length of the material reference[i] points at
sum of all referenced_size values == the total bytes between the end of the sidx box and the end of the last referenced subsegment
reference_type 0 for every reference whose target is a moof; 1 only when the target is a nested sidx

str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx stores each referenced_size and computes the subsegment boundaries by cumulative addition; a size that disagrees with the file makes the computed offsets fall outside the file, so fragment seeking resolves to nothing.
str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.notes: The 31-bit referenced_size is a byte count derived from the bytes the generator actually wrote for the referenced subsegments, never a pinned constant, and the NUMBER of references is free (see mp4box.reference_count).

str_sidx.subsegment_duration.tier_rationale: A duration is explicitly Tier C: it describes how long a subsegment plays and no decoder validates its magnitude against the media, so pinning it would remove timeline diversity from every fragmented file for no depth.
str_sidx.subsegment_duration.description: Duration of the referenced subsegment in the timescale given by the enclosing sidx box; any uint32 is legal, including 0.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.16.3.3: subsegment_duration is expressed in the timescale field of the SegmentIndexBox.

str_sidx.subsegment_duration.notes: Real files set this to the sum of the trun sample_duration values of the subsegment, but nothing checks that; a value of 0 or a very large value still parses.

str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.tier_rationale: The 3-bit SAP_type subfield is a finite enumeration (0-7, of which 1-6 are defined) that selects which stream-access-point interpretation the demuxer applies, and no decoder refuses the file over it; the remaining bits are a free 28-bit delta time, so the word is Tier B on its enumerated part.
str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.description: One sidx reference word packing a 3-bit SAP_type in bits 31-29, a 1-bit starts_with_SAP flag in bit 28 and a 28-bit SAP_delta_time in bits 27-0.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.16.3.3: starts_with_SAP (1 bit), SAP_type (3 bits) and SAP_delta_time (28 bits) share one 32-bit word; the .bt names the field after that packing.

str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.bit_layout: bits 31-29 = SAP_type: 1 closed GOP starting with an IDR, 2 closed GOP, 3 open GOP, 4 multi-level open GOP, 5 random access, 6 gradual decoding refresh, and 0 and 7 reserved. bit 28 = starts_with_SAP: 1 when the subsegment begins with a stream access point of the declared type. bits 27-0 = SAP_delta_time: presentation time of the first SAP minus presentation time of the first sample of the subsegment, in the sidx timescale.
bit_meanings: 0xE0000000 mask, SAP_type values 1-6 defined and 0 and 7 reserved
0x0FFFFFFF (268435455) mask for SAP_delta_time, a free 28-bit time value
str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.completeness_reason: The word has exactly three documented subfields and no reserved bits; SAP_type is the only enumerated part and all eight possible 3-bit values are listed in valid_values.
str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.decoder_gate: A decoder that trusts starts_with_SAP skips its own keyframe search for the subsegment; an unsupported SAP_type makes it fall back to scanning, which is a different and shallower path but not a refusal.
str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.notes: preferred_value 0x10000000 is starts_with_SAP=1, SAP_type=0, SAP_delta_time=0. Emitting SAP_type 1 through 6 covers every defined branch; 0 and 7 are reserved by the spec but still parse, so they are recorded here rather than dropped. SAP_delta_time itself is a free time value and must not be pinned.

mp4box.codingName.tier_rationale: A FourCC drawn from the open ISO/QuickTime codec registry that names the original unencrypted format; an unrecognised code does not make a demuxer refuse the file (it falls back to the enca/encv sample entry), so it is Tier B, not A.
mp4box.codingName.description: The frma (OriginalFormatBox) payload: the FourCC of the codec the sample entry would have carried before encryption was applied.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.2.2 (OriginalFormatBox): data_format is the four-character code of the original unencrypted sample entry, e.g. avc1, mp4a, hev1.

mp4box.codingName.completeness_reason: codingName may be any registered sample-entry FourCC; the list names the ones that actually occur in CENC-protected files and must be treated as representative, not as a closed set.

frma: codingName should equal the FourCC that the sibling enca/encv sample entry would have used unencrypted
frma is only meaningful inside a sinf box that also carries a schm box

mp4box.codingName.decoder_gate: A demuxer that does not recognise codingName keeps the stream's codec_id as the encrypted placeholder and reports an unknown codec, so the track is present but never decoded; that is a shallower path, not a refusal.
mp4box.codingName.notes: frma is the only case branch in the switch that has no version/flag prefix, because OriginalFormatBox is not a FullBox.

mp4box.version.tier_rationale: A per-box format version drawn from a tiny finite set that switches which optional members follow and how wide the time and offset fields are; the value itself is a registry entry, so Tier B, while the width agreement it implies is a Tier A structural obligation recorded per box below and in dependencies.
mp4box.version.description: The first byte of every FullBox payload: the layout version of that box type. It decides both the width of the time/offset fields that follow and which conditional members exist.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 4.2 (Box): every FullBox begins with an 8-bit version and 24-bit flags; the legal version of each box type is fixed by that box's own subclause.

mp4box.version.completeness_reason: No box type in ISO BMFF, CENC or QuickTime defines a version above 2, and the template only ever branches on version == 0 versus version > 0 (lines 506, 511, 528, 566, 602, 630, 656).

tenc: 0 or 1; version 0 writes reserved2 (506), version >= 1 writes default_crypt_skip_byte_block (507)
schm: 0 in ISO BMFF; 1 is the QuickTime variant
pssh: 0 or 1; version > 0 inserts KID_count and KID[] (530-534) before DataSize
senc: 0; version 1 adds pattern-encryption fields this template does not read
saio: 0 or 1; 0 makes offset[] uint32 (567), 1 makes it uint64 (569) - the width MUST match the bytes written
saiz: 0 or 1; no width change in this template
trun: 0 or 1; 0 makes sample_composition_time_offset uint32 (603), >= 1 makes it signed int32 (605), so the signedness must match what was written or negative CTS offsets are misread
sidx: 0 or 1; 0 makes earliest_presentation_time and first_offset uint32 (632-633), 1 makes them uint64 (637-638)
mehd: 0 or 1; 0 makes fragment_duration uint32 (657), 1 makes it uint64 (659)
elst: 0 only under this template - ISO version 1 widens segment_duration and media_time to 64 bits, but elst_entry (402-407) is uint32-only, so 1 desynchronises the box
mdhd: 0 only under this template - version 1 widens create_time, modify_time and duration to 64 bits, but they are read through the uint32-only mp4time struct (387) and a uint32 duration (746)
mvhd: 0 only under this template, for the same mp4time reason as mdhd
tkhd: 0 only under this template - version 1 widens create_time, modify_time and duration, which are read as 32-bit
ftyp: no version field; ftyp is not a FullBox

mp4box.version.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_default dispatches on the version byte for sidx, mehd, saio, trun, mdhd, mvhd, tkhd and elst and reads 32- or 64-bit fields accordingly; a version that disagrees with the widths actually written shifts every following field, the box size stops matching and the parser reports a corrupt file before any sample is reached.
mp4box.version.notes: The single highest-leverage Tier B field in the format: a small enumeration that silently changes the byte layout of the rest of the box. Because the template hard-codes 32-bit time fields, mdhd/mvhd/tkhd/elst have exactly one self-consistent emission, version 0 - a fact invisible unless the mp4time typedef at line 385 is read together with the case branches.

mp4box.flag.tier_rationale: These 24 bits are presence switches: each one decides whether a following member exists at all. A bit that disagrees with the bytes actually written shifts every subsequent field in the box, the declared box size stops matching the bytes consumed, and the demuxer rejects the file before reaching any sample - which is the Tier A test, not a Tier B registry lookup.
mp4box.flag.description: The 3-byte FullBox flag word that follows mp4box.version in almost every case branch, read big-endian as flag[0] (most significant), flag[1], flag[2] (least significant).

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 4.2: FullBox carries unsigned int(24) flags whose per-box meaning is defined in each box's subclause; the presence bits are the reason a wrong value is structural rather than cosmetic.

mp4box.flag.bit_layout: flag[2] holds bits 0-7 of the 24-bit word, flag[1] holds bits 8-15 and flag[0] holds bits 16-23. Every test the template performs is therefore written against flag[2] for the low byte and flag[1] for the middle byte.
bit_meanings: 0x000001 (flag[2] & 1) trun data-offset-present (line 591); tfhd base-data-offset-present (line 614); saio/saiz aux-info-type-present (lines 560, 574); schm scheme_version present (line 521 is read unconditionally, so this bit MUST be set); tenc default_constant_IV present

0x000002 (flag[2] & 2) tfhd sample-description-index-present (line 615); senc subsample-information-present - but the template tests 'flag[2] == 2' at line 546, an equality not a mask, so senc subsamples are only parsed when the whole word is exactly 2
0x010000 tfhd duration-is-empty (defined by ISO BMFF, not read by this template)
0x020000 tfhd default-base-is-moof (defined by ISO BMFF, not read by this template)
mp4box.flag.completeness_reason: These are all the flag bits ISO/IEC 14496-12 and ISO/IEC 23001-7 define for the box types this switch handles; for pssh, senc (other than 0x000002), mfhd, sidx, trex, mehd, stsd, enca, stts, stsc, stco, co64, stsz, stss and tenc the flags are reserved and must be 0.

tenc: reserved in version 0; CENC 3rd edition uses 0x000001 to signal a constant IV, which the template instead infers from default_per_sample_IV_size == 0
schm: 0x000001 MUST be set, because line 521 reads scheme_version unconditionally; clearing it makes the template consume 4 bytes that ISO BMFF says are absent
senc: 0 for no subsample data, exactly 2 (0x000002) for subsample data; the equality test at line 546 rejects any word that merely has bit 1 set among others
trun: any subset of 0x000001, 0x000004, 0x000100, 0x000200, 0x000400, 0x000800; each bit set adds the matching field to EVERY one of the sample_count entries, so the total entry size must be recomputed

mp4box.flag.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun, mov_read_tfhd, mov_read_saiz, mov_read_saio and mov_read_schm each build a local read mask from the flags and read exactly the fields the mask selects; a flag that claims a field which was not written, or hides one that was, makes the box's consumed byte count disagree with its size and mov_read_default reports 'overread' or leaves the track unusable.
mp4box.flag.notes: The .bt spelling is 'flag' (singular) for these 22 branches; the five branches that spell it 'flags' are keyed separately as mp4box.flags, and tkhd/vmhd use their own structs (tkhd_flags, vmhd_flags). The senc equality test at line 546 is a genuine template quirk: emitting flags 3 in a senc box silently drops the subsample table.

mp4box.flags.tier_rationale: A 24-bit FullBox flag word whose legal value is a single member of a finite set (0) for every box that spells it 'flags' in this template; no branch of the parser tests it, so a wrong value is not a structural failure, but the legal set is closed rather than open, which is Tier B rather than Tier C.
mp4box.flags.description: The 3-byte FullBox flag word of elst, hdlr, mdhd, mvhd and smhd; reserved and required to be 0 by ISO/IEC 14496-12 for all five.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclauses 8.6.6 (EditListBox), 8.4.3 (HandlerBox), 8.2.2 (MediaHeaderBox), 8.2.1 (MovieHeaderBox) and 12.1.3 (SoundMediaHeaderBox) all specify flags = 0.

mp4box.flags.completeness_reason: None of these five box types defines a single flag bit in ISO BMFF; QuickTime historically overloaded the hdlr word as component flags, but the template does not read them and no conforming demuxer branches on them.

hdlr: 0 (line 731); QuickTime component flags may be non-zero and are ignored

mp4box.flags.decoder_gate: No reader branches on these words, so a non-zero value is silently accepted; the file still decodes, which is exactly why this is Tier B and not Tier A.
mp4box.flags.notes: The tkhd and vmhd branches spell the same 3 bytes as a typed struct (tkhd_flags at line 777, vmhd_flags at line 794) and those DO carry meaning; see tkhd_flags.track_enabled and vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.

mp4box.reserved1.tier_rationale: A reserved byte that no reader tests; leaving it free adds entropy at zero depth cost, and pinning it would remove free variation without buying any decoder coverage.
mp4box.reserved1.description: Reserved byte of the tenc (TrackEncryptionBox) payload; ISO/IEC 23001-7 requires 0.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.3: the first byte after the FullBox header is reserved and shall be 0.

mp4box.reserved1.notes: Emitted as 0 in conforming files; any byte value still parses.

mp4box.reserved2.tier_rationale: A reserved byte (tenc) and a reserved 8-byte field (tkhd) that no reader tests; both are free.
mp4box.reserved2.description: Reserved byte of the tenc payload when version == 0; ISO/IEC 23001-7 requires 0. The tkhd spelling is a reserved 8-byte gap between duration and layer.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.3.2 (TrackHeaderBox) specifies two reserved fields of 4 and 8 bytes that shall be 0.

tenc: line 506, present only when version == 0; when version >= 1 the same byte position holds default_crypt_skip_byte_block instead
tkhd: line 783, 'uint64 reserved2', the 8-byte reserved gap after duration and before layer

mp4box.reserved2.notes: Two different fields share this spelling in the .bt, one 1 byte and one 8 bytes; both are reserved and both are free.

mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.tier_rationale: One byte packing two 4-bit pattern-encryption counters with a small closed legal set; a value outside that set makes a CENC decoder fall back to full-sample encryption rather than refuse the file, so it is Tier B.
mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.description: The tenc byte present only when version >= 1, packing crypt_byte_block in the high nibble and skip_byte_block in the low nibble of the pattern-encryption cycle.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 3rd edition subclause 9.3: TrackEncryptionBox version 1 carries crypt_byte_block and skip_byte_block as two 4-bit fields describing the pattern encryption cycle.

mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.bit_layout: bits 7-4 = crypt_byte_block, the number of 16-byte AES blocks encrypted in each pattern cycle. bits 3-0 = skip_byte_block, the number of 16-byte blocks left in clear. Zero in both nibbles means no pattern: the whole sample is encrypted.
bit_meanings: 0xF0 mask crypt_byte_block, legal 0-10 with 1 and 9 the commonest
mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.completeness_reason: The two nibbles give a raw space of 0-255, but only combinations with crypt_byte_block + skip_byte_block <= 10 describe a real pattern cycle; the listed values are the ones that occur plus the disabled case. Every byte 0-255 still parses.

tenc: present only when version >= 1; version == 0 takes the reserved2 branch at line 506 instead
crypt_byte_block + skip_byte_block should be at most 10, the pattern cycle length in 16-byte blocks

mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.decoder_gate: A CENC decoder that cannot honour the pattern decrypts the sample incorrectly and the picture is garbage, but the container still parses and the track is still exposed.
mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.notes: Reachable only from a tenc box with version >= 1, which lines 506-507 support.

mp4box.default_is_protected.tier_rationale: A one-byte boolean with the closed legal set {0, 1} that selects whether the track's samples are encrypted at all; a wrong value never causes refusal, so Tier B, but both states are distinct decoder branches and must both be emitted.
mp4box.default_is_protected.description: tenc field stating whether the track's samples are protected (encrypted) by the scheme declared in the enclosing sinf/schm box.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.3: IsProtected shall be 0 or 1.

tenc: 1 in any file that carries a sinf/schm/frma chain and real senc/saiz/saio data
0 means the tenc box is present but the track is in the clear, which is legal and exercises a different demuxer branch

mp4box.default_is_protected.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tenc stores the flag; when it is 0 the demuxer leaves the stream unencrypted and skips the whole CENC decryption setup, a genuinely different code path.
mp4box.default_is_protected.notes: Values other than 0 and 1 are undefined by the spec but still parse, so the closed set is a spec rule rather than a parser rule.

mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.tier_rationale: A finite registry of initialisation-vector widths {0, 8, 12, 16} that also gates whether the constant-IV fields follow; a value no reader recognises makes decryption fail but never makes the container refuse the file, so Tier B rather than A.
mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.description: tenc field giving the size in bytes of the per-sample initialisation vector carried in senc and sized by saiz; 0 means a constant IV is used instead.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.3: default_PerSampleIV_Size shall be 8 or 16 for per-sample IVs, or 0 when default_constant_IV is present instead.

mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.completeness_reason: CENC defines 8-byte and 16-byte IVs, the 3rd edition adds the 12-byte GCM IV, and 0 selects the constant-IV form; no other width is defined.

tenc: when 0, lines 513-514 must follow with default_constant_IV_size and that many default_constant_IV bytes
when 8 or 16, every senc entry's per_sample_IV must be that many bytes - this template always writes 8 at line 545
saiz default_sample_info_size must equal this value when the per-sample table is absent

mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tenc records the IV size and mov_read_senc and mov_read_saiz use it to slice the auxiliary data; a size that disagrees with the bytes present mis-slices every sample's encryption metadata, so decryption fails while parsing succeeds.
mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.notes: The template hard-codes 'byte per_sample_IV[8]' at line 545, so 8 is the only value that round-trips through this .bt without desynchronising senc; 16 is legal in the format and is recorded anyway.

mp4box.default_KID.tier_rationale: A 16-byte key identifier whose only real constraint is that it must match the KID advertised in the pssh boxes and the DRM licence; a mismatch makes the file unplayable at the licence stage but the container parses and the track is exposed, so it is not Tier A. It is Tier B because the field is a registered UUID-shaped identifier with a small set of conventional values, not an open numeric span.
mp4box.default_KID.description: The tenc 16-byte default key identifier (a UUID in big-endian byte order) naming the content key that protects this track's samples.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.3: default_KID is a 16-byte KeyID; ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 4.2 requires UUID-shaped identifiers to be written most-significant-byte first.

mp4box.default_KID.pattern: exactly 16 bytes, any value; conventionally a UUID with the version nibble set to 4 and the variant bits set, written big-endian. The same 16 bytes must appear in every pssh KID entry that refers to this track.
preferred_value: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 as 16 zero bytes is legal and common in test content

tenc: 16 bytes, always present, regardless of version

mp4box.default_KID.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tenc copies the KID into the stream's encryption side data and does not validate it; a KID that matches no licence only fails later, in the DRM layer, after the whole container has been parsed.
mp4box.default_KID.notes: Free 16 bytes as far as the parser is concerned; the constraint that matters is the agreement with pssh's KID entries, which is recorded in dependencies.

mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.tier_rationale: A byte count that sizes the immediately following default_constant_IV array; if it disagrees with the bytes written the tenc box is consumed at the wrong length, the enclosing sinf/schi chain desynchronises and the demuxer reports a corrupt box before any sample is read.
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.description: tenc field giving the number of bytes of default_constant_IV that follow it; present only when default_per_sample_IV_size == 0.
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.algorithm: byte count: default_constant_IV_size == number of default_constant_IV bytes emitted at line 514
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.covers: the default_constant_IV array that follows it

tenc: in practice 8 or 16, matching the AES-CTR or AES-CBC IV width, but any byte value is a legal count

mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tenc reads default_constant_IV_size and then that many bytes; a count larger than the bytes present makes it read past the end of the tenc box and mov_read_default reports an overread, dropping the track.
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.notes: The field is a byte-sized count, so it cannot express an IV longer than 255 bytes; that is a format limit, not a narrowing.

mp4box.default_constant_IV.tier_rationale: Opaque initialisation-vector bytes that no container parser inspects; constraining them would remove free entropy from every constant-IV CENC file without reaching any additional decoder code.
mp4box.default_constant_IV.description: The constant initialisation vector shared by every sample of the track, default_constant_IV_size bytes long.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.3: default_constant_IV is present when default_PerSampleIV_Size is 0 and is default_constant_IV_size bytes long.

mp4box.default_constant_IV.notes: The bytes are free; only the LENGTH is constrained, and that length is mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.

mp4box.scheme_type.tier_rationale: A FourCC drawn from the small closed CENC registry of protection schemes; each value selects a different decryption mode in the demuxer and an unrecognised one makes it skip protection handling rather than refuse the file, so it is Tier B with the full legal set recorded.
mp4box.scheme_type.description: The schm (SchemeTypeBox) FourCC naming the protection scheme applied to the track: cenc, cbc1, cens or cbcs.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.2.1: scheme_type shall be 'cenc' (AES-CTR full sample), 'cbc1' (AES-CBC full sample), 'cens' (AES-CTR pattern) or 'cbcs' (AES-CBC pattern).

mp4box.scheme_type.completeness_reason: These four CENC schemes are the complete ISO/IEC 23001-7 registry; 'drmi' is the legacy QuickTime FairPlay scheme and is included because the template is QuickTime-aware (it reads the QuickTime-only atoms at lines 37 and 151).

schm: scheme_type and scheme_version are read unconditionally at lines 520-521, so mp4box.flag must have 0x000001 set for this template's layout to match ISO BMFF
cens and cbcs require the tenc pattern fields at line 507, which only exist when tenc version >= 1

mp4box.scheme_type.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_schm stores the scheme and mov_read_tenc/mov_read_senc then choose CTR or CBC and full-sample or pattern decryption; an unrecognised scheme leaves the stream marked encrypted with no handler, so samples are delivered still encrypted.
mp4box.scheme_type.notes: 'cenc' is by far the commonest and reaches the deepest decryption setup, so it is the preferred value, but all five must be emitted.

mp4box.scheme_version.tier_rationale: A version number that no container parser validates and that selects no branch; by the tie-break rule a field arguable between B and C goes to C, and pinning it would remove free variation from every protected file for zero coverage.
mp4box.scheme_version.description: The schm field giving the version of the protection scheme named by scheme_type; conventionally 0x00010000 for the CENC schemes.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.2.1: scheme_version is present when the SchemeTypeBox flags indicate so and is 0x00010000 for cenc, cbc1, cens and cbcs.

mp4box.scheme_version.notes: Read unconditionally at line 521, which is why mp4box.flag must carry 0x000001 for this schm box. Any uint32 value parses.

mp4box.systemID.tier_rationale: A 16-byte UUID drawn from a small published registry of DRM systems; each recognised value makes the demuxer attach a different key-system side-data record, and an unrecognised one is skipped rather than fatal, so Tier B with every known value recorded.
mp4box.systemID.description: The pssh field naming the DRM system that the following Data blob belongs to, as a 16-byte UUID in big-endian order.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 8.1: SystemID is a 16-byte unique identifier of the DRM system; the published values are Widevine edef8ba9-79d6-4ace-a3c8-27dcd51d21ed, PlayReady 9a04f079-9840-4286-ab92-e65be0885f95, FairPlay 94ce86fb-07ff-4f43-adb8-93d2fa968ca2 and Common Key Request f239e769-efa3-4850-9c16-a903c6932efb.

mp4box.systemID.completeness_reason: The SystemID space is any 16-byte UUID; the five listed are the published DRM system identifiers that real demuxers compare against, and any other UUID is legal and simply unrecognised.

pssh: always 16 bytes, present in every pssh box
a file normally carries one pssh per DRM system it supports, all at the same level in moov or moof

mp4box.systemID.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_pssh matches the SystemID against its known key systems and, for PlayReady and Widevine, parses the Data blob to emit AVEncCommonEncryptionKeySystem side data; an unrecognised SystemID takes the skip branch, a shallower but still-executed path.
mp4box.systemID.notes: The 1077efec value is the W3C Clear Key system used by conformance suites; including it covers a fourth distinct demuxer branch.

mp4box.KID_count.tier_rationale: A count that sizes the KID[] array read immediately after it; if it disagrees with the number of 16-byte KIDs actually written, the pssh box is consumed at the wrong length, DataSize is then read from the wrong offset, and the enclosing moov desynchronises before any track is built.
mp4box.KID_count.description: The pssh field giving the number of 16-byte key identifiers that follow it; present only when version > 0.
mp4box.KID_count.algorithm: element count: KID_count == number of mp4box.KID 16-byte entries emitted at lines 531-534
mp4box.KID_count.covers: the KID_count anonymous structs of 16 bytes each that follow

pssh: when version == 0 the field and the whole KID array are absent and DataSize follows systemID directly

mp4box.KID_count.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_pssh loops KID_count times reading 16 bytes each and then reads DataSize; a count that overstates the written KIDs makes it consume DataSize's bytes as a KID, so the pssh Data blob is misread and the box overruns.
mp4box.KID_count.notes: The NUMBER of KIDs is a free choice of the generator; the Tier A obligation is only that the count written equals the number emitted.

mp4box.entry.tier_rationale: This spelling is the element (or the whole element array) of five different repeated tables, and in every one of them the bytes consumed must equal the count written times the element size; a disagreement shifts the file position, the enclosing box size stops matching, and the demuxer reports a corrupt box before any sample is decoded.
mp4box.entry.description: The repeated element of the pssh KID array, the senc per-sample record, the saiz per-sample info-size byte, the trun per-sample record and the stts/stsc run record.
mp4box.entry.field_type: byte[16] (pssh) / anonymous struct (senc, trun) / byte[sample_count] (saiz) / str_stts[] (stts) / str_stsc[] (stsc)
mp4box.entry.algorithm: element count times element size must equal the bytes emitted: the count is written in the enclosing box (KID_count, sample_count, entry_count) and the element layout is fixed by the box type
mp4box.entry.covers: the whole repeated element array of the enclosing box

pssh: line 533, 'byte entry[16]' inside the anonymous struct instantiated as KID[KID_count] at line 534; each element is exactly 16 bytes and there are KID_count of them
senc: line 555, the anonymous struct at lines 543-555 instantiated as entry[sample_count]; each element is 8 IV bytes plus, when flag == 2, a uint16 subsample_count and that many 6-byte subsample records
saiz: line 583, 'byte entry[sample_count]', present only when default_sample_info_size == 0; each element is one byte giving that sample's auxiliary info size
trun: line 607, the anonymous struct at lines 595-607 instantiated once per loop iteration; its size is 4 bytes per set presence bit, so all sample_count entries must be the same width
stts: line 679, 'str_stts entry[entry_count]'; element contents are specified by str_stts.sample_count and str_stts.sample_delta
stsc: line 685, 'str_stsc entry[entry_count]'; element contents are specified by str_stsc.first_chunk, str_stsc.samples_per_chunk and str_stsc.sample_description_index

mp4box.entry.decoder_gate: Every one of these arrays is read by a counted loop in ffmpeg (mov_read_pssh, mov_read_senc, mov_read_saiz, mov_read_trun, mov_read_stts, mov_read_stsc); an element width that disagrees with the flags or version desynchronises the loop and the box overruns its declared size.
mp4box.entry.notes: Five distinct .bt declarations share the spelling 'entry' because each sits in an anonymous struct or is a bare array, so the innermost named enclosing struct is mp4box itself. The NUMBER of elements is always free; only the agreement between the written count and the emitted elements is constrained.
