mp4box.DataSize.tier_rationale: A byte count of the pssh Data blob that follows; if it disagrees with the bytes written the pssh box is consumed at the wrong length and every sibling box after it in moov or moof is read from the wrong offset, so the demuxer fails structurally.
mp4box.DataSize.description: The pssh field giving the number of bytes of DRM system data that follow it.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 8.1: DataSize is the size in bytes of the Data field that follows.

mp4box.DataSize.algorithm: byte count: DataSize == number of mp4box.Data bytes emitted at line 537
mp4box.DataSize.covers: the mp4box.Data array that follows it

pssh: DataSize may legitimately be 0, in which case no Data bytes follow
DataSize must also leave the pssh box's total within boxheader.size

mp4box.DataSize.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_pssh allocates DataSize bytes and reads exactly that many, then checks the box end; a DataSize larger than the remaining box makes it log an overread and drop the pssh, and one smaller leaves the rest of the blob to be misparsed as the next box.
mp4box.DataSize.notes: This is the second of the two length fields in pssh, the other being KID_count; both must agree with the bytes written.

mp4box.Data.tier_rationale: This is an encoded payload: for Widevine a protobuf SignedMessage and for PlayReady a little-endian PlayReady Header Object. Random bytes here do not break the container parse, but the demuxer's DRM side-data branch is entered only when the blob is well formed, and that branch is otherwise unreachable code - the same depth-for-coverage trade the PNG IDAT entry makes.
mp4box.Data.description: The pssh payload: DataSize bytes of DRM-system-specific data whose internal encoding is fixed by the systemID that precedes it.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 8.1: Data carries system-specific information; Widevine defines it as a protobuf SignedMessage, PlayReady as a PlayReady Header Object, FairPlay as a CKC record.

mp4box.Data.codec_or_standard: DRM-system specific, selected by mp4box.systemID: Widevine protobuf; PlayReady Header Object (little-endian record header plus UTF-16LE XML); FairPlay CKC record
mp4box.Data.codec: Widevine: protobuf (field 1 'msg', length-delimited, wrapping an EncryptedMessage whose field 1 is the content_id string and field 3 the RSA-signature bytes). PlayReady: PlayReady Header Object, little-endian, RecordLength(uint32) RecordType(uint16) then a UTF-16LE XML header, terminated by RecordLength 0 and RecordType 0. FairPlay: CKC record with a 12-byte header and an encrypted content-id section.
mp4box.Data.must_produce: A blob whose encoding matches the systemID written at line 527. For Widevine: a single protobuf field with wire type 2 (length-delimited), tag byte 0x0A, a varint length, then a nested EncryptedMessage whose tag 0x0A introduces a length-prefixed ASCII content_id. For PlayReady: uint32 RecordLength equal to 4 + 2 + the byte length of the UTF-16LE XML that follows, uint16 RecordType 1, the XML, then uint32 0 and uint16 0 as the terminator. For FairPlay: the CKC 12-byte header with the correct length and version fields. DataSize must equal the byte length of whichever blob is written.
mp4box.Data.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_pssh copies DataSize bytes into an AVPacketSideData record of type AV_PKT_DATA_ENCRYPTION_INIT_INFO and, for the recognised key systems, runs the system-specific inner parse to extract the content id; random bytes make that inner parse fail and the side data is discarded, so the demuxer never executes its Widevine or PlayReady record-walking code. The container itself keeps parsing, so this is a depth loss rather than a refusal.
mp4box.Data.generation_strategy: Simplest correct construction, in order of preference. (1) Widevine protobuf with DataSize 0 is not possible, so use: pick systemID edef8ba9-79d6-4ace-a3c8-27dcd51d21ed, build the inner EncryptedMessage as bytes 0x0A <varint len> <ASCII content_id such as 'fftest'>, then wrap it as 0x0A <varint len of the inner message> <inner message>, and set DataSize to the total byte length. (2) PlayReady: take a short XML string such as '<WRMHEADER xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/DRM/2007/03/PlayReadyHeader" version="4.0.0.0"></WRMHEADER>', encode it UTF-16LE, prepend uint16 RecordType 1 and uint32 RecordLength = 4 + 2 + 2*len, append the terminator uint32 0 uint16 0, and set DataSize to the total. (3) The trivially valid fallback for any systemID: DataSize 0 and no Data bytes, which is legal and keeps the container well formed while sacrificing only the DRM branch. Never emit random bytes with a non-zero DataSize.

pssh: DataSize bytes long, immediately after DataSize

mp4box.Data.notes: The bytes INSIDE a well-formed blob (the content_id string, the XML text) are free; only the framing is Tier A. A file may carry several pssh boxes, one per DRM system, each with its own correctly encoded blob.

mp4box.sample_count.tier_rationale: A count that sizes a repeated table in four different boxes and that the demuxer cross-checks against the other sample tables; when the tables disagree the sample map cannot be built, the track is dropped and no sample is ever decoded, which is the Tier A test.
mp4box.sample_count.description: The number of samples described by the enclosing table: senc encryption records, saiz auxiliary-info sizes, trun run entries, or the whole stsz sample-size table.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.7.3.2 (SampleSizeBox) sample_count is the number of samples in the track; ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclauses 9.5 and 9.6 give the same meaning for senc and saiz; subclause 8.8.8 gives the number of samples in a trun.

mp4box.sample_count.algorithm: element count of the table that follows, and for stsz the total number of samples in the track, which must equal the sum of the stts run counts and the stsc-expanded per-chunk sample counts
mp4box.sample_count.covers: the repeated table that follows it in the same box

senc: line 542; number of per-sample encryption records, each 8 IV bytes plus the subsample table when flag == 2; must equal the number of samples in the enclosing traf
saiz: line 580; number of samples whose auxiliary info size is described; when default_sample_info_size != 0 no entry[] array follows, but sample_count still says how many samples the fixed size applies to
trun: line 590; number of samples in this run; the loop at line 593 reads exactly this many anonymous entry structs, so it must agree with the presence bits in mp4box.flag
stsz: line 703; total number of samples in the track; when sample_size != 0 no entry_size array follows, otherwise entry_size[sample_count] does

mp4box.sample_count.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stsz, mov_read_trun, mov_read_saiz and mov_read_senc each allocate and fill exactly sample_count slots and then verify the track's sample table against stts and stsc; a count that disagrees produces a short or overlong table, mov_read_trak fails and the track is never exposed to the codec.
mp4box.sample_count.notes: The NUMBER of samples is a free choice of the generator and a first-class diversity axis; the Tier A obligation is only that every table in the file states the same number and that the bytes emitted match it.

mp4box.per_sample_IV.tier_rationale: Opaque initialisation-vector bytes that no container parser inspects; constraining them would remove free entropy from every CENC file without reaching any additional decoder code.
mp4box.per_sample_IV.description: The senc per-sample initialisation vector, a fixed 8 bytes in this template.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.6: SampleEncryptionBox carries one IV per sample whose length is default_PerSampleIV_Size from the track's tenc box, 8 or 16 bytes.

senc: 8 bytes per sample here; the width is fixed by tenc default_per_sample_IV_size, which the template hard-codes to 8

mp4box.per_sample_IV.notes: The bytes are free; only the WIDTH is constrained, and that comes from mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size. Because line 545 hard-codes 8, emitting a tenc with a 16-byte IV desynchronises this template.

mp4box.subsample_count.tier_rationale: A count that sizes the subsample_data array read immediately after it inside each senc entry; if it disagrees with the records written, the next sample's IV is read from the wrong offset and the whole senc box desynchronises, so the demuxer fails structurally before any sample is decrypted.
mp4box.subsample_count.description: The senc per-sample count of subsample records that split the sample into clear and protected runs; present only when the senc flags word is exactly 2.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.6: when subsample information is present, each sample record carries a uint16 subsample_count followed by that many (uint16 bytes_of_clear_data, uint32 bytes_of_protected_data) pairs.

mp4box.subsample_count.algorithm: element count: subsample_count == number of mp4box.subsample_data 6-byte records emitted at line 553
mp4box.subsample_count.covers: the subsample_data array that follows it inside this senc entry

senc: present only when flag[2] == 2 (line 546, an equality test, not a mask)
0 is legal and means the whole sample is one protected run
for cbcs/cens pattern encryption the subsample split usually has one record per sample

mp4box.subsample_count.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_senc reads subsample_count and then that many 6-byte records per sample; a count that overstates the records consumes the next sample's IV bytes, so the senc box overruns and the track's encryption metadata is discarded.
mp4box.subsample_count.notes: The NUMBER of subsamples is free; the obligation is that it equals the records written and that their clear+protected bytes sum to the sample size.

mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.tier_rationale: Together with bytes_of_protected_data this partitions a sample's bytes; the CENC layer sums the partition and compares it against the sample size it obtained from trun or stsz, and a mismatch makes it reject the encrypted packet, so the sample is never delivered to the codec.
mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.description: The number of leading bytes of a subsample that are in the clear, before the AES-protected run begins.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.6: each subsample record is bytes_of_clear_data (16 bits) followed by bytes_of_protected_data (32 bits), and the two together must account for the whole subsample.

mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.algorithm: byte count: for every sample, sum over its subsamples of (bytes_of_clear_data + bytes_of_protected_data) == that sample's size from trun sample_size or stsz entry_size
mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.covers: the leading clear run of the subsample it describes

senc: 0 is legal and common: the whole subsample is protected
for H.264 and HEVC the clear run normally covers the NAL length prefixes and parameter sets

mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's CENC helper walks the subsample list and checks the accumulated clear+protected total against the packet size; a total that disagrees makes it log an invalid encrypted packet and drop the sample rather than feed garbage to the decoder.
mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.notes: This is the one place in the format where a wrong value does not corrupt the container but does corrupt the media path, which is exactly the kind of cross-validated field Tier A exists for.

mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.tier_rationale: The complement of bytes_of_clear_data in the same subsample partition; the CENC layer sums the partition against the sample size and rejects the packet when they disagree, so the sample never reaches the codec.
mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.description: The number of bytes of the subsample that are AES-encrypted, immediately following its clear run.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.6: bytes_of_protected_data is 32 bits so that a protected run may exceed 64 KiB, while the clear run is limited to 16 bits.

mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.algorithm: byte count: bytes_of_protected_data == subsample_length - bytes_of_clear_data, and the subsample lengths must sum to the sample's size
mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.covers: the trailing protected run of the subsample it describes

senc: 0 is legal and means the subsample is entirely in the clear
must be a multiple of the AES block size (16) when the scheme is cbc1 or cbcs, and unconstrained in length for cenc and cens

mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.decoder_gate: Same check as bytes_of_clear_data: ffmpeg's CENC helper validates the accumulated partition against the packet size and drops the sample on mismatch.
mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.notes: The 16-bit clear field next to a 32-bit protected field is the asymmetry a careless author would flatten to equal widths.

mp4box.subsample_data.tier_rationale: The repeated 6-byte subsample record array whose element count is written in subsample_count; a width or count disagreement desynchronises the senc entry loop, so the box overruns and the encryption metadata is discarded.
mp4box.subsample_data.description: The array of subsample records inside one senc entry, each a uint16 clear length and a uint32 protected length.
mp4box.subsample_data.algorithm: element count times 6 bytes: the array occupies subsample_count * 6 bytes inside this senc entry
mp4box.subsample_data.covers: the subsample_count records that follow subsample_count

senc: each record is exactly 6 bytes: uint16 then uint32

mp4box.subsample_data.decoder_gate: Read by the counted loop in ffmpeg's mov_read_senc; a record width that is not 6 bytes shifts every following sample record in the box.
mp4box.subsample_data.notes: The struct is anonymous in the .bt (lines 549-553), so its fields are keyed against mp4box directly.

mp4box.aux_info_type.tier_rationale: A FourCC drawn from the closed CENC registry naming which auxiliary info the saiz/saio table describes; an unrecognised value makes the demuxer ignore the table rather than refuse the file, so Tier B with the full legal set recorded.
mp4box.aux_info_type.description: The saiz/saio field, present only when the flags word has 0x000001 set, naming the type of sample auxiliary information the table carries.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclauses 9.5 and 9.7: aux_info_type shall be the four-character code of the encryption scheme, 'cenc', 'cbc1', 'cens' or 'cbcs'.

mp4box.aux_info_type.completeness_reason: These four CENC schemes are the complete registry ISO/IEC 23001-7 defines for sample auxiliary information; no other value is specified.

saio: line 562, present only when (flag[2] & 1) != 0 (line 560); followed by aud_info_type_parameter at line 563
saiz: line 576, present only when (flag[2] & 1) != 0 (line 574); followed by aux_info_type_parameter at line 577

mp4box.aux_info_type.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_saiz and mov_read_saio record the type and later match it against the track's schm scheme_type; a mismatch makes it ignore the auxiliary table, so the samples are delivered still encrypted.
mp4box.aux_info_type.notes: Should equal the scheme_type of the track's schm box. The saio branch misspells the following field as aud_info_type_parameter (line 563) while saiz spells it aux_info_type_parameter (line 577); both spellings are keyed separately below because the .bt identifiers differ.

mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.tier_rationale: A scheme parameter that no container parser validates and that selects no branch; by the tie-break rule a field arguable between B and C goes to C, and pinning it would remove free variation for zero coverage.
mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.description: The saio auxiliary-info-type parameter, present only when the flags word has 0x000001 set; always 0 for the four CENC schemes. The .bt misspells 'aux' as 'aud' in this branch only.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.7: aux_info_type_parameter is present whenever aux_info_type is and is 0 for cenc, cbc1, cens and cbcs.

mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.notes: The spelling difference from saiz's aux_info_type_parameter (line 577) is a typo in the .bt, not two distinct format fields; both are recorded because both identifiers appear in the template.

mp4box.aux_info_type_parameter.tier_rationale: A scheme parameter that no container parser validates and that selects no branch; see mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.
mp4box.aux_info_type_parameter.description: The saiz auxiliary-info-type parameter, present only when the flags word has 0x000001 set; always 0 for the four CENC schemes.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.5: aux_info_type_parameter is present whenever aux_info_type is and is 0 for cenc, cbc1, cens and cbcs.

mp4box.aux_info_type_parameter.notes: Correct spelling of the same field the saio branch misspells at line 563.

mp4box.entry_count.tier_rationale: A count that sizes a repeated table in eight different boxes; when it disagrees with the elements written the parser consumes the wrong number of bytes, the box size stops matching and the demuxer reports a corrupt file before any sample is decoded.
mp4box.entry_count.description: The number of entries in the table that follows: saio offsets, stsd sample entries, enca descriptions, stts runs, stsc runs, stco/co64 chunk offsets or stss sync samples.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclauses 8.6.1 (stsc), 8.6.1.1 (stts), 8.6.2 (stco/co64), 8.6.2.1 (stss), 8.5.2 (stsd) and ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.7 (saio) all define entry_count as the number of records that follow.

mp4box.entry_count.algorithm: element count: entry_count == number of table elements emitted immediately after it, each of the width that box type defines
mp4box.entry_count.covers: the whole repeated table that follows it in the same box

saio: line 565; number of offsets, one per auxiliary-info item, each uint32 when version == 0 and uint64 when version == 1
stsd: line 665; number of sample entries, each a full mp4box with its own size and FourCC; must be >= 1 for a decodable track
enca: line 672; the template then reads a fixed 0x14 bytes at line 673 regardless, so entry_count here is decorative for this .bt
stts: line 678; number of str_stts runs; their sample_counts must sum to the stsz sample_count
stsc: line 684; number of str_stsc runs; their first_chunk values must be increasing and inside the chunk table
stco: line 690; number of uint32 chunk offsets, one per chunk
co64: line 696; number of uint64 chunk offsets, one per chunk; used instead of stco when any offset exceeds 4 GiB
stss: line 712; number of uint32 sync-sample numbers; 0 or an absent stss means every sample is a sync sample

mp4box.entry_count.decoder_gate: Each table is read by a counted loop in ffmpeg (mov_read_saio, mov_read_stsd, mov_read_stts, mov_read_stsc, mov_read_stco, mov_read_stss); a count larger than the elements present makes the loop read past the box, and a smaller one leaves the rest of the box to be misparsed as the next box.
mp4box.entry_count.notes: The NUMBER of entries is a free choice of the generator and a first-class diversity axis; the Tier A obligation is only that the count written equals the elements emitted, plus the cross-table agreements listed per box.

mp4box.offset.tier_rationale: A byte offset from the start of the file to a sample auxiliary information item; a wrong offset sends the demuxer to unrelated bytes, the per-sample encryption metadata is garbage, and the track cannot be decrypted, so no useful work is done on the media path.
mp4box.offset.description: The saio field giving the file-relative byte offset of each auxiliary info item, uint32 when version == 0 and uint64 when version == 1.

evidence.note: The version branch is at line 566 (if(version == 0)) with uint64 offset[entry_count] at line 569. ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.7: SampleAuxiliaryInformationOffsetsBox holds entry_count offsets, each 32 bits when version is 0 and 64 bits when version is 1.

mp4box.offset.offset_from: the first byte of the file
mp4box.offset.algorithm: byte offset: offset == absolute file position of the auxiliary info item for that sample, i.e. the position of its senc entry as it will sit in the final file
mp4box.offset.covers: the auxiliary info region belonging to one sample

saio: entry_count offsets, one per sample that has auxiliary info
version 1 (uint64) is required when any offset exceeds 4 GiB
the offsets must be strictly increasing in sample order

mp4box.offset.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_saio stores the offsets and the CENC path seeks to them to read each sample's IV; an offset that lands outside the senc data yields an IV of unrelated bytes, so every sample fails decryption.
mp4box.offset.notes: Width selection is driven by mp4box.version, so a version that disagrees with the widths written shifts every following offset in the table.

mp4box.default_sample_info_size.tier_rationale: A byte width drawn from a small closed set that gates whether the per-sample entry[] array follows; a value outside the set makes the auxiliary info unreadable rather than making the container refuse the file, so Tier B with the legal widths recorded.
mp4box.default_sample_info_size.description: The saiz field giving the size in bytes of every sample's auxiliary information when they are all the same; 0 means the per-sample entry[] array follows instead.

evidence.note: The zero-test is at line 581 (if(default_sample_info_size == 0)). ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.5: if default_sample_info_size is not 0 every sample has that many bytes of auxiliary info and no per-sample table follows; if it is 0, sample_count bytes follow.

mp4box.default_sample_info_size.completeness_reason: 0 is mandated by the spec and any non-zero byte is syntactically legal; the values listed are the ones that correspond to a real CENC auxiliary-info layout, 8 and 16 being the IV widths from tenc default_per_sample_IV_size.

saiz: line 579; when 0 the entry[sample_count] byte array at line 583 must follow
when non-zero no array follows and sample_count at line 580 says how many samples the fixed size applies to
must equal tenc default_per_sample_IV_size for a consistent CENC track

mp4box.default_sample_info_size.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_saiz takes the fixed-size branch or allocates and reads sample_count bytes; a fixed size that disagrees with tenc's IV size makes the CENC layer read the wrong number of IV bytes per sample.
mp4box.default_sample_info_size.notes: 0 versus non-zero is a real two-way branch in both the .bt and the demuxer, so both must be emitted.

mp4box.data_offset.tier_rationale: A signed byte offset that tells the demuxer where this run's samples start; a wrong offset makes it read sample bytes from an unrelated part of the file, the packets are malformed NAL or audio frames and the codec refuses them, so no useful work is done.
mp4box.data_offset.description: The trun field giving the byte offset from the first byte of the enclosing moof to the first sample of this run; present only when flag bit 0x000001 is set.
mp4box.data_offset.field_type: uint32 (read as signed int32 by demuxers)

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.8: data_offset is a signed 32-bit integer giving the offset of the first sample of this run, relative to the base-data-offset of the containing track fragment (which defaults to the first byte of the enclosing moof).

mp4box.data_offset.offset_from: the first byte of the enclosing moof box (more precisely tfhd base_data_offset, which defaults to the moof start)
mp4box.data_offset.algorithm: byte offset: data_offset == (absolute file position of this run's first sample byte) - (absolute file position of the enclosing moof's first byte)
mp4box.data_offset.covers: the contiguous run of sample payloads this trun describes

trun: for the first trun of a fragment the offset normally lands just after the moof, i.e. inside the mdat that follows
consecutive truns in one traf must tile the media without gaps or overlaps

mp4box.data_offset.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun stores data_offset and mov_read_trak computes each sample's absolute position as base_data_offset + data_offset + accumulated sizes; a value that points outside mdat makes every packet short or zero-length, so av_read_frame returns errors and no frame is decoded.
mp4box.data_offset.notes: The template declares it uint32 but demuxers interpret it as signed so that a run may point backwards into an earlier moof; a generator that only emits unsigned values still covers the common forward case.

mp4box.first_sample_flags.tier_rationale: A closed 32-bit sample-flags bitfield; each bit is separately tested by the demuxer to decide sync-ness and dependency, but a wrong combination yields a bad seek point rather than an unparseable file, so Tier B with the full field layout recorded.
mp4box.first_sample_flags.description: The trun field overriding the sample flags of the run's first sample only; present only when flag bit 0x000004 is set.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.3 defines the 32-bit sample_flags layout; subclause 8.8.8 says first_sample_flags applies to the first sample of the run and overrides the per-sample flags and the tfhd defaults.

bit_layout.name: is_leading
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not a leading sample

bit_layout.name: sample_depends_on
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 does not depend (a sync sample), 2 depends, 3 reserved

bit_layout.name: sample_is_depended_on
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 not depended on, 2 depended on, 3 reserved

bit_layout.name: sample_is_non_sync_sample
bit_layout.meaning: 1 means not a sync sample, 0 means sync

valid_values: 0x00000000 or 0x01000000 for a sync first sample
mp4box.first_sample_flags.completeness_reason: The bit_layout above is the complete 32-bit sample_flags definition of ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.3; every field of it is listed.

trun: the common use is to mark the first sample of a fragment as a random-access point, i.e. sample_depends_on = 1 and sample_is_non_sync_sample = 0

mp4box.first_sample_flags.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun applies these bits to its first sample's flags and mov_read_stss/mov_build_index uses sample_depends_on and sample_is_non_sync_sample to build the keyframe index; wrong bits make seeking land on a non-decodable frame, but the container parses.
mp4box.first_sample_flags.notes: A single field whose meaning is the whole 32-bit layout, not a value to pin.

mp4box.sample_duration.tier_rationale: A presentation duration in the media timescale; no container parser validates it and it selects no branch, so by the tie-break rule it is Tier C. Only its PRESENCE is constrained, and that is governed by mp4box.flag.
mp4box.sample_duration.description: The trun per-sample duration in the track's media timescale units; present only when flag bit 0x000100 is set, and inherited from tfhd default_sample_duration or trex when absent.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.8: sample-duration is optional per sample and overrides the default; subclause 8.8.5 gives trex default_sample_duration.

trun: one per sample, so all sample_count entries must carry it or none

mp4box.sample_duration.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun copies the duration into its sample table and uses it to derive presentation timestamps; a value of 0 makes consecutive samples share a timestamp, which players tolerate, and a huge value makes the track appear long. Neither stops parsing.
mp4box.sample_duration.notes: A duration is a Tier C quantity by the tier policy; the sum over a fragment should equal the fragment's total for a realistic file, but that is a quality note, not a constraint a decoder enforces.

mp4box.sample_size.tier_rationale: A byte length that bounds how many bytes the demuxer pulls out of mdat for each sample; a value that disagrees with the media makes it emit truncated or over-long packets, which the codec rejects outright, so no frame is decoded.
mp4box.sample_size.description: The size in bytes of one sample: the trun per-sample size when present, or in stsz either 0 (a per-sample entry_size table follows) or a uniform size applying to every sample of the track.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.8 (TrackRunBox sample-size) and subclause 8.7.3.2 (SampleSizeBox: sample_size 0 means the per-sample table follows, otherwise every sample is that many bytes).

mp4box.sample_size.algorithm: byte count: each sample_size must equal the number of media bytes that sample actually occupies in mdat, so sum(sample_size) over a run == the run's byte span; in stsz, when sample_size != 0 the total media bytes == sample_size * sample_count, and when sample_size == 0 the entry_size array must sum to the total media bytes
mp4box.sample_size.covers: one sample's payload inside mdat (trun) or every sample of the track (stsz)

trun: line 598, present only when flag & 0x000200; one per sample
stsz: line 702, always present; 0 selects the entry_size[sample_count] array at line 706, non-zero means uniform sizes and no array

mp4box.sample_size.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun and mov_read_stsz fill the sample-size table and mov_read_packet slices mdat with it; a size larger than the remaining mdat bytes truncates the packet and a smaller one leaves the next sample starting mid-frame, so the bitstream is malformed and decoding fails.
mp4box.sample_size.notes: This is the field most often got wrong by naive generators: the value must come from the media the generator actually wrote, not from a constant. Uniform-size stsz (sample_size != 0) is a genuine second mode worth emitting.

mp4box.sample_flags.tier_rationale: A closed 32-bit sample-flags bitfield whose individual bits the demuxer reads to build the keyframe and dependency tables; a wrong combination produces a bad seek index rather than an unparseable file, so Tier B with the complete field layout recorded.
mp4box.sample_flags.description: The trun per-sample override of the sample flags; present only when flag bit 0x000400 is set, otherwise inherited from tfhd default_sample_flags or trex.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.3 defines the sample_flags layout; subclause 8.8.8 lists sample-flags as an optional per-sample field of TrackRunBox.

bit_layout.name: is_leading
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 leading, 2 not leading, 3 not a leading sample

bit_layout.name: sample_is_depended_on
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 not depended on, 2 depended on, 3 reserved

mp4box.sample_flags.completeness_reason: The layout above is the complete sample_flags definition of ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.3.

trun: must agree with the stss sync-sample table when the track also carries one

mp4box.sample_flags.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun stores per-sample flags and mov_build_index derives keyframes from sample_depends_on and sample_is_non_sync_sample; a track marked all-sync makes every frame a seek point, a track marked none-sync makes seeking impossible, but the container parses either way.
mp4box.sample_flags.notes: The same 32-bit layout appears as mp4box.first_sample_flags (line 592), mp4box.default_sample_flags (lines 618 and 651).

mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.tier_rationale: A presentation-versus-decode time offset; no container parser validates it and it selects no branch. Only its WIDTH is constrained, and that is governed by mp4box.version.
mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.description: The trun per-sample composition time offset in media timescale units, uint32 when version == 0 and signed int32 when version == 1 so that B-frame reordering can move a sample earlier; present only when flag bit 0x000800 is set.

evidence.note: The version branch is at line 602 (if(version == 0)) with int32 sample_composition_time_offset at line 605. ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.8: sample-composition-time-offsets is 32 bits unsigned for version 0 and signed for version 1; a signed value is required whenever B-frames reorder presentation before decode.

trun: version 1 with negative values is the correct encoding for H.264 or HEVC streams that contain B-frames

mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trun adds the offset to each decode timestamp to get the presentation timestamp; an unsigned version-0 offset cannot express a negative shift, so B-frame order is wrong but the file still parses and decodes.
mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.notes: Version 1 must be used whenever the track reorders; emitting version 0 with a large unsigned offset is the classic naive mistake.

mp4box.trackID.tier_rationale: A cross-validated identifier: the tfhd and trex trackID must equal the track_id of an existing trak's tkhd. When it does not, the demuxer cannot attach the fragment to any track and drops the whole moof, so no sample of that fragment is ever decoded - that is the Tier A test.
mp4box.trackID.description: The identifier of the track a tfhd or trex box describes; it must name a track declared by a tkhd box elsewhere in the file.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.5 (TrackExtendsBox) and 8.8.7 (TrackFragmentHeaderBox) both define track_ID as referring to the track_id of a TrackBox in the same file; subclause 8.3.2 says track_id values must be unique and non-zero within a movie.

mp4box.trackID.algorithm: cross-reference: tfhd.trackID and trex.trackID must equal some tkhd.track_id in the same moov; every trak that will receive fragments needs exactly one matching trex in mvex
mp4box.trackID.covers: the whole tfhd/trex box and every trun beneath it

tfhd: line 613, always present, the first field after the FullBox header
trex: line 647, always present; mvex must contain one trex per track that any moof will reference

mp4box.trackID.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tfhd looks the track up with mov_find_stream_by_track_id and logs 'could not find corresponding track' when it is absent, returning an error that discards the fragment; mov_read_trex stores the defaults under the same lookup.
mp4box.trackID.notes: 0 is illegal: track_id values start at 1 and mvhd next_track_id must be greater than every track_id used.

mp4box.base_data_offset.tier_rationale: A file-relative byte offset that every trun data_offset is measured from; a wrong value sends the demuxer to unrelated bytes for the entire fragment, the packets are malformed and the codec rejects them, so no useful work is done.
mp4box.base_data_offset.description: The tfhd field giving the absolute file offset of the base from which the trun data_offset values of this fragment are measured; present only when flag bit 0x000001 is set.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.7: base-data-offset-present selects an explicit base; when absent the base is the first byte of the enclosing Movie Fragment Box, and for the first traf in a moof that is the first byte of the moof itself.

mp4box.base_data_offset.offset_from: the first byte of the file
mp4box.base_data_offset.algorithm: byte offset: base_data_offset == absolute file position from which each trun data_offset is measured, normally the first byte of the enclosing moof; absolute sample position == base_data_offset + data_offset + accumulated sample sizes
mp4box.base_data_offset.covers: every trun data_offset inside this traf

tfhd: when the bit is clear the implicit base is the moof start, which is what nearly every real file uses

mp4box.base_data_offset.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tfhd sets frag->base_data_offset from this field when the flag is present and otherwise to the moof start; a value that does not point at the media makes every sample position wrong and every packet unreadable.
mp4box.base_data_offset.notes: Emitting the explicit form (flag bit set) and the implicit form (bit clear) covers two distinct demuxer branches; the implicit form is by far the more common.

mp4box.sample_description_index.tier_rationale: A 1-based index into the track's stsd entry table; a value of 0 or one greater than entry_count makes the demuxer dereference a missing sample entry, the track has no codec parameters and is dropped before any sample is decoded.
mp4box.sample_description_index.description: The tfhd field selecting which stsd sample entry the fragment's samples use; present only when flag bit 0x000002 is set.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.7: sample-description-index is a 1-based index into the SampleEntry array of the track's stsd box; subclause 8.5.2 says the index must be between 1 and entry_count.

mp4box.sample_description_index.algorithm: 1-based index: 1 <= sample_description_index <= stsd.entry_count of the track named by mp4box.trackID
mp4box.sample_description_index.covers: the sample entry that supplies the codec configuration for this fragment

tfhd: 1 is correct for the overwhelmingly common single-entry stsd

mp4box.sample_description_index.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_tfhd checks the index against the track's stsd count and logs an out-of-range error, discarding the fragment; mov_read_trex applies the same check to the default.
mp4box.sample_description_index.notes: Zero-based is the classic off-by-one here; every sample_description_index in the format is 1-based.

mp4box.default_sample_description_index.tier_rationale: The trex standing default for the same 1-based stsd index; an out-of-range value leaves every fragment of the track without codec parameters, so no sample is decoded.
mp4box.default_sample_description_index.description: The trex field giving the default 1-based stsd sample-entry index for fragments of this track that do not override it.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.5: default_sample_description_index is a 1-based index into the track's SampleEntry array and must be between 1 and entry_count.

mp4box.default_sample_description_index.algorithm: 1-based index: 1 <= default_sample_description_index <= stsd.entry_count of the track named by mp4box.trackID
mp4box.default_sample_description_index.covers: every tfhd of this track that clears its sample-description-index flag

trex: line 648, always present, the field after trackID

mp4box.default_sample_description_index.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trex stores the default and mov_read_tfhd falls back to it when the tfhd flag is clear; an out-of-range default breaks every fragment of that track.
mp4box.default_sample_description_index.notes: Always 1 for a normal single-codec track.

mp4box.default_sample_duration.tier_rationale: A duration in media timescale units; no container parser validates it and it selects no branch, so by the tie-break rule it is Tier C. Only its PRESENCE in tfhd is constrained, and that is governed by mp4box.flag.
mp4box.default_sample_duration.description: The standing default duration for samples of the track that do not carry their own, declared in trex and optionally overridden per fragment in tfhd.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.5 (TrackExtendsBox) and 8.8.7 (TrackFragmentHeaderBox, optional default-sample-duration) both define this field.

mp4box.default_sample_duration.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trex and mov_read_tfhd store the default and mov_read_trun applies it to samples that carry no duration; a value of 0 makes every sample share a timestamp, which players tolerate.
mp4box.default_sample_duration.notes: Commonly timescale / framerate, e.g. 1024 for a 44100 Hz audio track or timescale/25 for 25 fps video, but any uint32 parses.

mp4box.default_sample_size.tier_rationale: A byte length the demuxer falls back on to slice mdat when a trun omits per-sample sizes; a value that disagrees with the media produces malformed packets that the codec rejects, so no frame is decoded.
mp4box.default_sample_size.description: The standing default size in bytes of every sample of the track that carries no size of its own, declared in trex and optionally overridden per fragment in tfhd.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.5 (TrackExtendsBox) and 8.8.7 (TrackFragmentHeaderBox, optional default-sample-size) both define this field; subclause 8.8.8 says a trun sample-size overrides it.

mp4box.default_sample_size.algorithm: byte count: default_sample_size must equal the byte length of every sample the fragment describes when no trun sample_size and no stsz entry_size is present
mp4box.default_sample_size.covers: each sample payload of fragments that inherit this default

trex: line 650, always present; 0 is common for video because sizes always vary

mp4box.default_sample_size.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trex and mov_read_tfhd store the default and mov_read_trun applies it to samples without a size; a non-zero default that does not match the media mis-slices every packet in the fragment.
mp4box.default_sample_size.notes: A non-zero default is realistic only for fixed-rate audio; for video 0 with explicit trun sizes is the correct encoding.

mp4box.default_sample_flags.tier_rationale: A closed 32-bit sample-flags bitfield inherited by every sample that carries no flags of its own; wrong bits produce a bad keyframe index rather than an unparseable file, so Tier B with the full layout recorded.
mp4box.default_sample_flags.description: The standing default sample flags for the track, declared in trex and optionally overridden per fragment in tfhd.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.3 defines the sample_flags layout; subclauses 8.8.5 and 8.8.7 define default_sample_flags in TrackExtendsBox and TrackFragmentHeaderBox.

bit_layout.name: is_leading
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 leading, 2 not leading, 3 not a leading sample

bit_layout.name: sample_is_depended_on
bit_layout.meaning: 0 unknown, 1 not depended on, 2 depended on, 3 reserved

valid_values: 0x02000000 for a default of dependent non-sync samples
0x00000000 for a default of independent sync samples
mp4box.default_sample_flags.completeness_reason: The layout above is the complete sample_flags definition of ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.3.
mp4box.default_sample_flags.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_trex and mov_read_tfhd store the default and mov_build_index uses it for samples with no per-sample flags; a default that marks every sample sync produces an unusable seek index but a parseable file.
mp4box.default_sample_flags.notes: Most encoders put 0x02000000 in trex (all samples dependent) and use trun first_sample_flags 0x00000000 to mark each fragment's first sample as a random-access point.

mp4box.sequence_number.tier_rationale: A cross-validated counter: every mfhd sequence_number must be unique and increasing across the file's moof boxes, and mfra/tfra random-access records address fragments by it. A duplicate or non-increasing value makes the fragment order ambiguous and seeking into the fragment fails, so the file is only partly usable.
mp4box.sequence_number.description: The mfhd field giving the ordinal of this movie fragment, counting from 1 and increasing by exactly 1 for each subsequent moof.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.4: sequence_number 'intuitively defines the order of movie fragments'; subclause 8.8.11 (TrackFragmentRandomAccessBox) addresses fragments by tfra_time and by moof sequence number, so the numbering must be stable and increasing.

mp4box.sequence_number.algorithm: running counter: the first moof of the file carries sequence_number 1 and each later moof increments it by 1; no value may repeat
mp4box.sequence_number.covers: the ordering of every moof in the file

mfhd: line 623, always present, the only payload field after the FullBox header
exactly one mfhd per moof, as its first child

mp4box.sequence_number.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_mfhd records the number in its fragment index and mov_read_mfra uses it to resolve tfra random-access entries; a repeated or backwards number makes the mfra lookup ambiguous so seeking lands on the wrong fragment, though linear playback still works.
mp4box.sequence_number.notes: 0 is legal for a file with no mfra but unconventional; the reliable encoding is 1, 2, 3, ... in moof order.

mp4box.referenceID.tier_rationale: A cross-validated identifier: the sidx referenceID must name an existing track or a moof, otherwise the index cannot be attached to any stream and the demuxer discards it, losing all subsegment seeking.
mp4box.referenceID.description: The sidx field naming the stream the index refers to: the track_ID of a track, or 0 when the index refers to the movie fragment that follows it.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3: reference_ID is the track_ID of the reference stream, or 0 if the index describes the following movie fragment(s).

mp4box.referenceID.algorithm: cross-reference: referenceID == 0, or == the trackID of a track declared by a tkhd and, for fragmented files, present in mvex trex
mp4box.referenceID.covers: the whole reference[] table that follows the sidx header

sidx: line 628, always present, the first field after the FullBox header

mp4box.referenceID.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx records the reference ID and matches it against its stream list when building the seek index; an ID that names no stream leaves the sidx unattached, so subsegment seeking is unavailable while linear playback continues.
mp4box.referenceID.notes: 0 is the commonest value in DASH files, where the sidx sits immediately before the moof it indexes.

mp4box.timescale.tier_rationale: A cross-validated units field: the sidx timescale must equal the time_scale of the mdhd of the stream the index refers to. When it does not, every subsegment_duration and earliest_presentation_time in the index is interpreted in the wrong units, seeking lands in the wrong place and the index is worse than absent.
mp4box.timescale.description: The sidx field giving the number of time units per second used by the index's earliest_presentation_time and subsegment_duration values.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3: timescale 'is an integer that specifies the number of time units per second... if the Segment Index is located within a track, this field shall be the same as the timescale of the referenced track'.

mp4box.timescale.algorithm: units equality: sidx.timescale == mdhd.time_scale of the track named by referenceID (or of the movie when referenceID == 0)
mp4box.timescale.covers: the units of earliest_presentation_time and of every str_sidx.subsegment_duration in this sidx

sidx: line 629, always present, the field after referenceID

mp4box.timescale.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx converts subsegment_duration into the stream's time base using this value when building its seek index; a mismatched timescale scales every index entry wrongly, so seeks land far from the requested time.
mp4box.timescale.notes: The value space is open (any positive uint32) but the constraint is a closed equality against mdhd, which is why this is Tier A and mp4box.time_scale is Tier B.

mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.tier_rationale: A presentation timestamp; no container parser validates it and it selects no branch, so by the tier policy timestamps are Tier C. Only its WIDTH is constrained, and that is governed by mp4box.version.
mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.description: The sidx field giving the presentation time of the first subsegment the index describes, in timescale units; uint32 when version == 0 and uint64 when version == 1.

evidence.note: The version branch is at line 631 (if(version == 0)) with uint32 first_offset at 633 and the 64-bit pair earliest_presentation_time / first_offset in the else arm from line 636. ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3: earliest_presentation_time is 32 bits for version 0 and 64 bits for version 1; version 1 exists for files longer than the 32-bit span at the given timescale.

sidx: lines 630-639, always present; version 1 doubles both this field and first_offset to 64 bits

mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx stores it as the base presentation time of the first indexed subsegment; a value far from the media's real start shifts the whole seek index in time but the file still parses and plays.
mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.notes: 0 is the correct value for the first sidx of a file whose media starts at presentation time 0.

mp4box.first_offset.tier_rationale: A byte offset from the first byte after the sidx box to the first referenced byte; a wrong value sends the demuxer to unrelated bytes for the whole indexed region, so the fragment it points at cannot be read and seeking into it produces nothing decodable.
mp4box.first_offset.description: The sidx field giving the distance in bytes from the end of this sidx box to the first byte of the first referenced item, normally the start of the moof that follows; uint32 when version == 0, uint64 when version == 1.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3: first_offset is 'the distance in bytes, in the file containing the Segment Index, between the first byte of the first referenced item and the position immediately after the Segment Index'; subclause 8.11.3.1 says each reference's referenced_size is likewise a byte count from the end of the previous referenced item.

mp4box.first_offset.offset_from: the first byte after the end of the enclosing sidx box
mp4box.first_offset.algorithm: byte offset: first_offset == (absolute file position of the first referenced byte) - (absolute file position immediately after the sidx box's last byte); 0 is correct when the referenced moof starts right after the sidx
mp4box.first_offset.covers: the first referenced item, normally the following moof plus its mdat

sidx: lines 633 and 638, always present immediately after earliest_presentation_time
0 is the normal value in DASH and fMP4 files where the sidx directly precedes the moof

mp4box.first_offset.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx adds first_offset to the position just past the sidx to locate the first subsegment; a non-zero wrong value makes every subsequent referenced_size accumulate from a bad base, so all index entries point outside the media.
mp4box.first_offset.notes: The sidx is the only box in this format whose offsets are relative to the end of the box itself rather than to the start of the file, which is exactly the kind of asymmetry a naive generator flattens.

mp4box.time_scale.tier_rationale: An open positive-integer field, but its legal values are effectively a registry of conventional media clock rates and it is the denominator of every timestamp in the file, so a generator should draw from the conventional set rather than from the whole uint32 range; a value no clock matches still parses, which is why this is Tier B and not Tier A.
mp4box.time_scale.description: The mdhd and mvhd field giving the number of media (or movie) time units per second; every duration and timestamp in the box is expressed in these units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 time_scale <name="Time Scale", comment="Number of media time units per second">;
evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.2.2 (MediaHeaderBox) and 8.2.1 (MovieHeaderBox) define timescale as the number of time units per second; the template's own comment at lines 745 and 755 states the same.

mp4box.time_scale.pattern: any uint32 greater than 0; the conventional values are the media clock rates below. A sidx that indexes this track must repeat the value in its own timescale field.
mp4box.time_scale.completeness_reason: Any positive uint32 is syntactically legal and new codecs introduce new rates; the listed values are the ones real encoders emit and the ones demuxers are tuned for.

mdhd: line 745; the track's media clock, e.g. 90000 for MPEG video, 44100 or 48000 for audio, 1000 or the frame-rate multiple for raw H.264
mvhd: line 755; the movie clock, conventionally 600 (QuickTime) or 1000

mp4box.time_scale.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_mdhd stores time_scale and derives st->time_base from it; mov_read_mdhd explicitly guards against a non-positive value and falls back to 1, so 0 is survivable but silently rescales the whole track.
mp4box.time_scale.notes: 0 must still be emittable as a fuzzing value even though it is meaningless, because the clamping branch is real demuxer code.

mp4box.reference_count.tier_rationale: A count that sizes the str_sidx reference array read immediately after it; if it disagrees with the records written the sidx box is consumed at the wrong length and the next box after it is read from the wrong offset, so the demuxer fails structurally.
mp4box.reference_count.description: The sidx field giving the number of 12-byte reference records that follow it.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3: reference_count is a 16-bit unsigned integer giving the number of references, each of which is a Reference of 12 bytes.

mp4box.reference_count.algorithm: element count: reference_count == number of mp4box.references str_sidx records emitted at line 642, each exactly 12 bytes
mp4box.reference_count.covers: the str_sidx reference array that follows it

sidx: line 641, always present; 0 is legal and means the sidx indexes nothing
the field is 16 bits, so a sidx cannot index more than 65535 items

mp4box.reference_count.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx loops reference_count times reading 12 bytes each; a count that overstates the records makes it read past the end of the sidx and misparse whatever follows as a box.
mp4box.reference_count.notes: The NUMBER of references is free and is a diversity axis; the obligation is only that the count equals the records written.

mp4box.references.tier_rationale: The repeated 12-byte reference record array whose element count is written in reference_count and whose referenced_size values are byte offsets into the following media; a width or count disagreement desynchronises the sidx and every box after it.
mp4box.references.description: The array of sidx reference records, each a reference type and 31-bit size, a subsegment duration and a starts-with-SAP field.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3: each Reference is reference_type (1 bit) + referenced_size (31 bits) + subsegment_duration (32 bits) + starts_with_SAP (1 bit) + SAP_type (3 bits) + SAP_delta_time (28 bits), 12 bytes in total.

mp4box.references.algorithm: element count times 12 bytes: the array occupies reference_count * 12 bytes, and the sum of the referenced_size values plus mp4box.first_offset must span exactly the bytes the sidx indexes
mp4box.references.covers: the reference_count str_sidx records that follow reference_count

sidx: line 642; the .bt marks the array open=suppress so a count that exceeds the box is not flagged by this template, but a real demuxer still overruns

mp4box.references.decoder_gate: Read by the counted loop in ffmpeg's mov_read_sidx, which accumulates each referenced_size into an absolute offset; a record that is not 12 bytes shifts every following record and every index entry points at the wrong place.
mp4box.references.notes: Element contents are specified by the three str_sidx.* entries; this entry covers the array's existence and total span.

mp4box.reserved.tier_rationale: Reserved padding bytes and words that no reader tests; leaving them free adds entropy at zero depth cost, and pinning them would remove free variation without buying any decoder coverage.
mp4box.reserved.description: The reserved gap fields of sidx, mvhd, smhd and tkhd; ISO/IEC 14496-12 requires all of them to be 0.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.11.3 reserves the 16 bits before reference_count; subclause 8.2.1 reserves 10 bytes in MovieHeaderBox; subclause 12.1.3 reserves the 16 bits after balance in SoundMediaHeaderBox; subclause 8.3.2 reserves 4 bytes after track_ID and 8 bytes after duration in TrackHeaderBox.

sidx: line 640, the uint16 immediately before reference_count
mvhd: line 759, 'byte reserved[10]' between preferred_volume and matrix_structure
tkhd: line 781, the uint32 between track_id and duration

mp4box.reserved.decoder_gate: No reader inspects these bytes; ffmpeg skips them, so any value parses. Only their WIDTH matters, because a wrong width shifts every field after them in the same box.
mp4box.reserved.notes: Conforming files emit 0. The four widths are fixed by the spec and by the .bt declarations, so the width is not a free parameter even though the bytes are. See also mp4box.reserved2 for tkhd's 8-byte gap and mp4box.reserved3 for tkhd's third gap.

mp4box.fragment_duration.tier_rationale: A duration in movie timescale units; no container parser validates it and it selects no branch, so by the tier policy durations are Tier C. Only its WIDTH is constrained, and that is governed by mp4box.version.
mp4box.fragment_duration.description: The mehd field giving the total duration of the whole fragmented presentation in mvhd time_scale units; uint32 when version == 0 and uint64 when version == 1.

evidence.note: The version branch is at line 656 (if(version == 0)) with uint64 fragment_duration in the else arm at line 659. ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.8.2: fragment_duration is 32 bits for version 0 and 64 bits for version 1, and gives the duration of the whole movie including all fragments.

mehd: lines 656-659, always present; mehd is an optional child of mvex

mp4box.fragment_duration.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_mehd stores the value and uses it to set the total duration of a fragmented file before all fragments have been seen; a wrong value makes the reported duration wrong and the progress bar inaccurate, but playback is unaffected.
mp4box.fragment_duration.notes: Version 1 exists for live or very long presentations whose total exceeds the 32-bit range at the movie timescale.

mp4box.entries.tier_rationale: The repeated element array of two different boxes, sized by a count written immediately before it; a disagreement between count and elements shifts the file position so the enclosing stsd or elst box overruns its declared size and the demuxer reports a corrupt file before any sample is decoded.
mp4box.entries.description: The array of child records: in stsd a list of full sample-entry boxes (one per codec), in elst a list of edit-list segments.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.5.2: SampleDescriptionBox holds entry_count SampleEntry boxes, each with its own size and format FourCC; subclause 8.6.6: EditListBox holds entry_count EditEntry records of 12 bytes each.

mp4box.entries.algorithm: element count: stsd emits entry_count complete mp4box sample entries whose sizes sum to the stsd content size minus 8; elst emits num_entries 12-byte elst_entry records
mp4box.entries.covers: the whole child array of the enclosing box

stsd: line 667; each element is a full box with boxheader.size, boxheader.type and a codec-specific body (avc1, hvc1, mp4a, enca, tx3g and friends)
the commented-out 'str_stsd description[entry_count]' at line 666 is the dead alternative; this mp4box recursion is the live path
entry_count must be >= 1 for a decodable track, and every sample_description_index in stsc or tfhd must point inside it
elst: line 719; each element is an elst_entry of duration, media_time and media_rate, 12 bytes

mp4box.entries.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stsd loops entry_count times, each iteration reading a nested box header and dispatching on its FourCC; a child size that overruns the stsd makes it log 'invalid size' and abandon the track, leaving the file with no streams.
mp4box.entries.notes: The stsd case is where the format's codec diversity lives: every distinct sample-entry FourCC in valid_values of boxheader.type is reachable only from here.

mp4box.data.tier_rationale: A fixed 20-byte blob that this template reads opaquely but that really carries the QuickTime AudioSampleEntry fields a demuxer uses to configure the audio decoder; a garbage blob yields nonsense codec parameters and an unusable track rather than an unparseable file, so Tier B with the real layout recorded.
mp4box.data.description: The enca (EncryptedAudioSampleEntry) body: 20 fixed bytes holding the QuickTime audio sample-entry fields version, revision, vendor, channelcount, samplesize, compressionID, packetSize and samplerate.

evidence.note: QuickTime File Format Specification, Sound Sample Description: after the 8-byte SampleEntry header come version (16 bits), revision level (16), vendor (32), number of channels (16), sample size (16), compression ID (16), packet size (16) and sample rate (32, 16.16 fixed) - 20 bytes in total, exactly the 0x14 the template reads.

mp4box.data.pattern: 20 bytes laid out as: uint16 version (0 or 1), uint16 revision_level (0), uint32 vendor (0), uint16 channelcount (1 or 2), uint16 samplesize (8 or 16), uint16 compressionID (0), uint16 packetSize (0), uint32 samplerate as a 16.16 fixed-point value (e.g. 44100 << 16 = 0xAC440000)
preferred_value: version 0, revision 0, vendor 0, channelcount 2, samplesize 16, compressionID 0, packetSize 0, samplerate 0xAC440000

enca: line 673, read after entry_count at line 672; the template's enca branch is a QuickTime-style layout and does not match ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 12.1.1 exactly, but the 20-byte body it reads is the QuickTime one

mp4box.data.decoder_gate: A real demuxer reading an 'enca' sample entry takes the audio branch and pulls channel count, sample size and sample rate from these bytes to configure the decoder before the frma/tenc chain tells it the original codec; zero or absurd values leave the audio track with no valid parameters, so it is skipped while the container parses.
mp4box.data.notes: The bytes are fixed-layout, not free: channelcount 0 or samplerate 0 makes the entry unusable. The original codec of an enca entry is carried by the frma codingName in the enclosing sinf, not here.

mp4box.chunk_offset.tier_rationale: File-relative byte offsets to the start of each chunk of media; the demuxer seeks to them to read every sample. A wrong offset makes it pull bytes from unrelated parts of the file, so the packets are malformed and the codec rejects them - no frame is decoded.
mp4box.chunk_offset.description: The stco (uint32) or co64 (uint64) table of absolute file offsets, one per chunk, giving where each chunk's first sample begins.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.7.5: ChunkOffsetBox holds entry_count chunk offsets, 32 bits each; ChunkLargeOffsetBox (co64) is identical but with 64-bit offsets and exists because the 32-bit form cannot address past 4 GiB.

mp4box.chunk_offset.offset_from: the first byte of the file
mp4box.chunk_offset.algorithm: byte offset: chunk_offset[i] == absolute file position of the first byte of chunk i (chunk numbering is 1-based in stsc); offsets must be strictly increasing, each must lie inside an mdat box, and chunk i's byte span must equal the sum of the sample sizes that str_stsc assigns to it, so chunk_offset[i+1] >= chunk_offset[i] + span(i)
mp4box.chunk_offset.covers: one chunk's contiguous run of samples inside mdat

stco: line 691, uint32 per entry; must not be used when any offset is >= 2^32
co64: line 697, uint64 per entry; the only legal form once the file exceeds 4 GiB

mp4box.chunk_offset.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stco fills the chunk-offset array and mov_build_index derives every sample's absolute position from it plus the accumulated sample sizes inside the chunk; an offset outside mdat makes each packet read return short data, so decoding never starts.
mp4box.chunk_offset.notes: stco and co64 are mutually exclusive in a well-formed stbl: emit exactly one of them. Choosing co64 over stco is a distinct demuxer branch worth covering.

mp4box.entry_size.tier_rationale: The per-sample byte lengths the demuxer uses to slice mdat; a value that disagrees with the media produces truncated or over-long packets that the codec rejects outright, so no frame is decoded.
mp4box.entry_size.description: The stsz per-sample size table, present only when sample_size == 0; sample_count uint32 values giving each sample's length in bytes.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.7.3.2: when sample_size is 0, sample_count entry sizes follow, each a 32-bit unsigned integer giving that sample's size in bytes.

mp4box.entry_size.algorithm: byte count: entry_size[i] == number of bytes sample i occupies in mdat; the array must sum to the total media bytes, and the per-chunk sums must match the chunk_offset spacing

stsz: line 706, inside the 'if(sample_size == 0)' block at line 704; exactly sample_count entries, present only in that mode

mp4box.entry_size.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stsz fills sc->sample_sizes and mov_read_packet uses them to bound every read from mdat; a size larger than the bytes left truncates the packet and a smaller one leaves the next sample starting mid-frame, so the elementary stream is malformed and decoding fails.
mp4box.entry_size.notes: These values must be derived from the media actually written, never synthesised; 0 is legal and means an empty sample, which real encoders use for audio priming.

mp4box.sample_number.tier_rationale: A 1-based index into the track's sample table; a value of 0 or one greater than stsz sample_count makes the demuxer mark a non-existent sample as a keyframe, corrupting the seek index so that seeking produces an undecodable start point.
mp4box.sample_number.description: The stss table of 1-based sample numbers identifying the sync samples (keyframes) of the track.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.6.2.1: SyncSampleBox lists entry_count sample numbers, each 1-based and strictly increasing; when the box is absent every sample is a sync sample.

mp4box.sample_number.algorithm: 1-based index: 1 <= sample_number[j] <= stsz.sample_count, strictly increasing in j, and each must name a sample the codec can actually start from (an IDR frame for H.264/HEVC, any frame for intra-only codecs)
mp4box.sample_number.covers: the sync-sample subset of the track's sample table

stss: line 713, entry_count entries; an stss with entry_count 0 or an absent stss means every sample is a sync sample
must agree with the sample_depends_on bits of trun sample_flags and tfhd default_sample_flags when the track is fragmented

mp4box.sample_number.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_stss builds the keyframe list and mov_build_index marks those samples as seekable start points; a number beyond sample_count is clamped or ignored, so seeking to that point lands on a dependent frame that cannot be decoded on its own.
mp4box.sample_number.notes: The NUMBER of sync samples is free; the 1-based numbering is the classic off-by-one trap, since every other index in the sample tables is also 1-based.

mp4box.num_entries.tier_rationale: A count that sizes the elst_entry array read immediately after it; a disagreement shifts the file position so the elst box overruns its declared size and the enclosing edts/trak is misparsed, leaving the track unusable.
mp4box.num_entries.description: The elst field giving the number of 12-byte edit-list segments that follow it.
mp4box.num_entries.algorithm: element count: num_entries == number of elst_entry records emitted at line 719, each exactly 12 bytes (uint32 duration + uint32 media_time + fp32 media_rate)
mp4box.num_entries.covers: the whole elst_entry array that follows it

elst: line 718; 0 entries is legal and means an empty edit list that removes all media from the track
the sum of the entry durations should equal the track duration in mvhd time_scale units

mp4box.num_entries.decoder_gate: ffmpeg's mov_read_elst loops num_entries times reading 12 bytes each and builds the trim/delay entries from them; a count larger than the records makes it read past the elst box, and the box size check then fails.
mp4box.num_entries.notes: The .bt spells this 'num_entries' while every other table in the template uses 'entry_count'; both spellings are separate keys because the identifiers differ.

mp4box.major_brand.tier_rationale: A FourCC drawn from the registered brand list of ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.4 and the QuickTime specification; the demuxer uses it to choose parsing conventions, and a brand outside the registry makes it apply the wrong conventions rather than refuse the file, so Tier B with every brand a real reader branches on recorded.
mp4box.major_brand.description: The ftyp field naming the specification the file conforms to most closely; it must be one of the brands also listed in compatible_brand.

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.4: major_brand identifies the specification the file is most conformant to; registered brands include 'isom', 'iso2', 'iso4', 'iso5', 'iso6', 'avc1', 'mp41', 'mp42', 'dash', 'msdh', 'msix', 'cmfc', 'M4V ', 'M4A ', 'M4B ', 'qt  ', '3gp4', '3gp5', '3g2a', 'mj2s'.

If a fixed encoded elementary stream is used, the correct move is to write the coded geometry into the sample entry and let tkhd width/height vary freely, or to derive the sample entry's geometry from the chosen tkhd width - not to restrict tkhd width to the few values a precomputed payload happens to match. mp4box[type=\"mdat\"].payload.description: The content region of an mdat box: the concatenated media samples of every track, addressed only through stco/co64 chunk offsets plus stsc grouping plus stsz sizes, or through trun data_offset plus per-sample sizes in a fragmented file.

mp4box[type=\"mdat\"].payload.codec: Selected per track by the sample-entry FourCC in stsd: H.264/AVC (avc1, avc3) as length-prefixed NAL units, HEVC (hvc1, hev1) as length-prefixed NAL units, MPEG-4 Visual (mp4v) as visual object units, AAC-LC (mp4a) as raw access units framed by AudioSpecificConfig with NO ADTS header, AC-3/E-AC-3 (ac-3, ec-3) as sync frames, ALAC (alac), Opus (Opus) as raw packets with no Ogg framing, VP8/VP9 (vp08, vp09) as length-prefixed frames, AV1 (av01) as temporal units of length-prefixed OBUs, timed text (tx3g, stpp, wvtt) as 3GPP text samples or XML/WEBVTT documents, and the CENC-encrypted forms of all of these (enca, encv) where the sample is ciphertext over the same layout.
mp4box[type=\"mdat\"].payload.must_produce: For each track, exactly sample_count samples laid end to end inside mdat, where sample i occupies exactly the byte range the sample tables compute for it and its length equals the value written for it. Each sample must be one complete, independently parseable access unit of that track's codec. For H.264 and HEVC that means a sequence of NAL units each preceded by a length prefix whose width is lengthSizeMinusOne+1 bytes as declared in avcC/hvcC (4 bytes in practice), the NAL unit types being legal for the stream (SPS and PPS live in avcC, VPS/SPS/PPS in hvcC, and are not repeated in every sample; each video sample starts with an IDR or non-IDR slice NAL, optionally preceded by an AUD; each length counts only the NAL payload, not the prefix), and the sum of prefix+NAL lengths over the sample equals the declared sample size exactly. For AAC it means one raw frame whose length equals the declared sample size and whose AudioSpecificConfig in esds matches the track's sampling frequency and channel configuration. For CENC-encrypted samples it means the same layout with the protected byte ranges ciphertext, the leading bytes_of_clear_data of each senc subsample left in clear, and a per_sample_IV of the declared size reachable through saio/saiz.
mp4box[type=\"mdat\"].payload.generation_strategy: Build the media first and the tables from it, never the reverse. (1) Pick the track's codec from the sample-entry FourCC you intend to write into stsd. (2) Emit real access units, either by driving a real encoder or by drawing from a real precomputed elementary stream, one per sample, and record each unit's byte length as you go. (3) Write those recorded lengths into stsz (sample_size 0 plus the entry_size array) or into trun sample_size, and write the absolute byte offset of each chunk's first sample into stco/co64 - or, for a fragmented file, write trun data_offset relative to the moof that describes it. (4) Set the mdat boxheader.size to the actual byte count of everything written. (5) To get more samples, emit more access units: the sample count and the individual sizes stay free, and no size is ever chosen to match a payload that already existed. For an encrypted variant, run the same construction and then encrypt the protected byte ranges according to the senc subsample split, keeping bytes_of_clear_data in clear and making the sum of clear+protected over all subsamples equal the sample size.

mdat: reached through the default branch at line 799; named in the BoxName registry at line 212
a file may hold one mdat for the whole movie, or one mdat after each moof in a fragmented presentation; every chunk_offset and every data_offset must point inside some mdat

mp4box[type=\"mdat\"].payload.decoder_gate: ffmpeg resolves each sample to an mdat byte range from stco+stsc+stsz, or from trun in a fragment, and hands exactly those bytes to the codec parser. h264 rejects a length prefix that does not match the bytes available, the AAC decoder rejects a frame whose length disagrees with the sample size, and in every such case it logs a decode error and emits no output frames. If the bytes are random the container still parses and the demuxer still reports streams, but coverage stops at the parser entry point and none of the pixel or audio pipeline executes.
mp4box[type=\"mdat\"].payload.notes: This entry and mp4box[type="stsd"].sample_entry are the only two payload_wellformedness constraints in the format and they carry all of its depth, because the container itself is a size/FourCC tree with no checksum and no compression. mdat content is NOT free. mdat may legally appear before or after moov; when it appears first, stco offsets must still be absolute file offsets, so the generator must either fix the layout up front or patch the offsets in a second pass.

mp4box[type=\"stsd\"].sample_entry.tier_rationale: This is where the file learns which decoder to instantiate. The bytes are read by the template as a nested mp4box (line 667) whose type falls through to 'default: FSkip(contentsize)' at line 799, so the codec-specific body is never named; but a demuxer that cannot read a real SampleEntry with a real codec configuration child produces a stream with codec_id NONE and decodes nothing. Tier A, and the second of the format's two payload_wellformedness constraints.
mp4box[type=\"stsd\"].sample_entry.description: The body of one sample-entry box inside stsd: the 8-byte box header, the 6 reserved bytes and 2-byte data_reference_index of SampleEntry, the codec-specific fixed fields, and the codec configuration child boxes.
mp4box[type=\"stsd\"].sample_entry.field_type: byte[entry size - 8] inside a nested mp4box (no declared field name)

evidence.note: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.5.2 defines SampleEntry and the VisualSampleEntry/AudioSampleEntry derivations; ISO/IEC 14496-15 subclauses 5.3.3.1 and 8.3.3 define the avcC and hvcC configuration records; ISO/IEC 14496-14 subclause 5.6 and ISO/IEC 14496-3 subclause 4.4.1 define esds and AudioSpecificConfig.

mp4box[type=\"stsd\"].sample_entry.codec_or_standard: ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.5.2 SampleEntry / VisualSampleEntry / AudioSampleEntry layout plus the codec configuration children defined by ISO/IEC 14496-15, 14496-14 and 14496-3, and the sinf subtree of ISO/IEC 23001-7

mp4box[type=\"stsd\"].sample_entry.must_produce: A structurally complete SampleEntry. Common prefix: 8-byte box header (size, FourCC), 6 reserved bytes of 0, then a 2-byte data_reference_index that is 1-based and points at an entry of the dref box in the same track's dinf. Video (VisualSampleEntry, ISO/IEC 14496-15 subclause 5.3.3): uint16 pre_defined 0, uint16 reserved 0, uint32[3] pre_defined2 all 0, uint16 width and uint16 height as the CODED pixel dimensions, uint32 horizresolution 0x00480000 (72 dpi), uint32 vertresolution 0x00480000, uint32 reserved 0, uint16 frame_count 1, byte compressorname[32] whose first byte is the length of the name that follows and whose remaining bytes are name then zero padding, uint16 depth 0x0018, int16 pre_defined -1, then the codec configuration child boxes. Audio (AudioSampleEntry, ISO/IEC 14496-14 subclause 5.6): uint16 channelcount, uint16 samplesize, uint16 pre_defined 0, uint16 reserved 0, uint32 samplerate as a 16.16 fixed-point value (for example 44100 << 16 = 0xAC440000), then esds. Every configuration child must itself be a well-formed box with a correct size and FourCC, and for avcC/hvcC must carry real NAL parameter sets whose declared geometry agrees with the width and height written in the entry.
mp4box[type=\"stsd\"].sample_entry.generation_strategy: Choose the codec first, then emit that codec's entry: write the 8-byte header with the entry FourCC, the fixed fields above carrying the geometry (video) or the channel count and sample rate (audio) you actually want, then append the configuration child - a real avcC containing a real SPS and PPS, a real hvcC containing real VPS/SPS/PPS, or a real esds containing a real AudioSpecificConfig - as a nested box with its own correct size, and finally set the entry's boxheader.size to the byte count of everything written. The coded width and height inside the entry, the SPS geometry, and the mdat sample payloads must all describe the same picture size; derive the configuration from the dimensions you chose, and vary the dimensions by regenerating the configuration rather than by restricting the dimension field. entry_count is the free axis that says how many alternative codecs a track offers.

mp4box[type=\"free\"].content.generation_strategy: Fill with arbitrary bytes - zero, random, or a repeated pattern - and size the box header to match.
