These thirteen types are pure containers: their content is nothing but nested boxes read in a loop bounded by the parent's endOffset (lines 472-496), so a container must contain whole boxes that tile its content region exactly.

stsd is the one container whose children are counted rather than looped: line 667 reads exactly entry_count nested mp4box sample entries, so entry_count must equal the number of sample-entry boxes actually written.
In stsz, a sample_size of 0 is the signal that samples have differing sizes and an entry_size array of sample_count uint32 values follows (lines 704-707).
A non-zero stsz sample_size means every sample has that same size and no entry_size array is present; writing one anyway shifts every later table and desynchronises the parse.
tenc version 0 has a reserved byte where version 1 and later carry default_crypt_skip_byte_block (lines 506-507).
tenc version 1 replaces that reserved byte with default_crypt_skip_byte_block, the number of leading clear bytes in every sample (ISO/IEC 23001-7 subclause 9.2).
In tenc, a zero per-sample IV size means the track uses a constant IV, so default_constant_IV_size followed by exactly that many bytes of default_constant_IV must be present (lines 511-515).
A non-zero per-sample IV size means senc carries an IV per sample and the constant-IV fields are absent; emitting them inserts bytes the parser does not expect and misaligns the rest of tenc.
pssh version 1 or later carries a KID_count and that many 16-byte key IDs; version 0 carries none and goes straight to DataSize (lines 528-537).

saio and saiz carry aux_info_type and aux_info_type_parameter only when the low bit of the 24-bit flags word is set (lines 560-564 and 574-578); the template tests flag[2] & 1 because flag is a big-endian byte[3] whose third byte holds the low 8 bits.
In saiz, a default_sample_info_size of 0 means the per-sample auxiliary-information sizes differ and an array of sample_count single bytes follows (lines 581-584).
saio stores its offsets as uint32 when version is 0 and as uint64 otherwise (lines 566-569); the width is forced by the version byte and getting it wrong shifts every offset value.
senc carries subsample information per sample only when the flags word equals 2 (useSubsampleEncryption, lines 546-554); otherwise each of the sample_count entries is just the 8-byte per_sample_IV.

trun data-offset-present (0x000001, tested as flag[2] & 1 at line 591): the single int32 data_offset follows sample_count and locates this run's samples relative to the base data offset of the enclosing moof.

trun first-sample-flags-present (0x000004, tested as flag[2] & 4 at line 592): a uint32 sample-flags word that overrides the default for the first sample of the run only, typically marking it a sync sample.

trun sample-duration-present (0x000100, tested as flag[1] & 1 at line 597): every one of the sample_count entries carries its own uint32 duration; when the bit is clear the trex default_sample_duration applies instead.

trun sample-size-present (0x000200, tested as flag[1] & 2 at line 598): every entry carries its own uint32 size, which is what a fragmented file uses instead of stsz to locate sample bytes inside mdat.
trun sample-flags-present (0x000400, tested as flag[1] & 4 at line 599): every entry carries its own uint32 flags word instead of inheriting the default.

trun sample-composition-time-offsets-present (0x000800, tested as flag[1] & 8 at line 600): every entry carries a composition offset, the fragmented equivalent of ctts, and without it presentation order equals decode order.

trun version 0 stores the composition offset unsigned; version 1 stores it as a signed int32 so that negative offsets (B-frame reordering that puts presentation before decode) are expressible (lines 602-605).
The signed form is the only way to express a negative composition offset; a decoder that sees version 1 reads the same four bytes as int32, so the two versions are not interchangeable.

tfhd base-data-offset-present (0x000001, line 614): a uint64 absolute file offset that all trun data_offset values in this traf are relative to; when the bit is clear the base is the first byte of the enclosing moof.
tfhd sample-description-index-present (0x000002, line 615): overrides the trex default_sample_description_index for this fragment.
tfhd default-sample-duration-present (0x000008, line 616): the duration applied to every sample of this fragment that does not carry its own trun sample_duration.
tfhd default-sample-size-present (0x000010, line 617): the size applied to every sample of this fragment that does not carry its own trun sample_size.
tfhd default-sample-flags-present (0x000020, line 618): the flags word applied to every sample of this fragment that does not carry its own trun sample_flags.

sidx version 0 stores earliest_presentation_time and first_offset as uint32; version 1 stores both as uint64 (lines 630-639). The version byte decides the width of two adjacent fields, so a mismatch shifts referenceID-relative parsing of the whole reference array.
The 64-bit form is required for presentations longer than 2^32 timescale units, or whose first referenced segment starts beyond the 4 GiB file offset.
mehd stores fragment_duration as uint32 for version 0 and uint64 for version 1 (lines 656-659).

stco holds 32-bit chunk offsets and co64 holds 64-bit ones (lines 687-698); the two are mutually exclusive inside stbl and the choice is forced by the magnitude of the offsets the generator has to write.
Any chunk beyond the 4 GiB file offset cannot be expressed in stco, so co64 becomes mandatory; a decoder reading stco would wrap the offset and point at the wrong bytes of mdat.

ISO/IEC 14496-12 makes creation_time, modification_time and duration 64-bit in version 1 of mvhd/mdhd/tkhd and 32-bit in version 0. NOTE the template's mp4time is hardcoded to uint32 (line 387), so it only parses version 0 correctly; a real decoder handles both, and this rule is recorded from the spec so the generator can choose either version consistently rather than mixing widths.

elst version 1 entries are uint64 segment_duration, int64 media_time, int32 media_rate_integer, int16 media_rate_fraction (20 bytes); version 0 entries are uint32, int32, int16, int16 (12 bytes) which is what elst_entry at lines 402-407 declares. The template implements version 0 only.

A language value below 0x400 is one of the QuickTime macintosh language codes the enum at lines 38-150 lists; ReadLang (lines 276-288) prints it via EnumToString. hdlr's component subtype names the media handler and selects which media-information header the minf must contain: 'vide' requires vmhd, 'soun' requires smhd, 'hint' requires hmhd, and 'meta'/'text'/'subt'/'sbtl'/'tmcd' require nmhd or gmhd. A mismatch makes ffmpeg attach the wrong stream type or reject the track.
Audio tracks carry smhd (balance plus reserved, lines 769-774) and must not carry vmhd; the AudioSampleEntry in stsd must then supply channelcount and samplerate consistent with the mdhd time_scale.

A QuickTime-branded file may use the QuickTime-only atoms and the QuickTime language, graphics-mode, matrix and opcolor tables the template cites at lines 37 and 151; an ISO-branded file should stick to the ISO box set. Both remain legal to emit.

ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 4.3 requires the major brand to be repeated among the compatible brands, so that a reader supporting only the compatible list still accepts the file; ffmpeg warns when the brand list contradicts itself but continues.

then.equals: the track_id of one of the moov's trak boxes
then.count: one trex per track that will appear in a fragment

dependencies.reason: Declaring mvex promises the movie is fragmented; every trex.trackID must match exactly one tkhd.track_id, and every track that appears in a moof must have a trex, otherwise the fragment has no defaults and ffmpeg drops it.

then.equals: the previous moof's sequence_number plus 1, starting at 1

dependencies.reason: mfhd.sequence_number orders the fragments; ffmpeg uses it to detect missing fragments and to decide whether a traf has already been seen. A repeated or decreasing number makes it skip or re-order fragments.

then.equals: the track_id declared in some trak's tkhd inside moov

dependencies.reason: A track fragment binds to a track only through this ID; if it matches nothing, ffmpeg logs 'could not find track' and the whole moof contributes no samples, so all the mdat bytes addressed by its trun are never decoded.

then.max: the stsd entry_count of the same track

dependencies.reason: Sample description indexes are 1-based into the enclosing track's stsd entries array (line 667); 0 or a value above entry_count makes ffmpeg report 'invalid sample description index' and the track yields no decoder.

A CENC protection scheme requires a TrackEncryptionBox in schi carrying the default key ID, IV size and crypt-skip block; without it ffmpeg cannot initialise its CENC decryption path and the encrypted samples stay ciphertext.

then.equals: the codec FourCC the samples really carry, e.g. mp4a or avc1

dependencies.reason: frma (original format box, line 499-501) inside the encrypted entry's sinf must name the underlying codec, because that is the only place a decoder learns what to instantiate once it has decrypted; a wrong codingName makes ffmpeg pick the wrong parser and fail on the first sample.

then.equals: the sum of str_stts.sample_count over every entry of the same track's stts

dependencies.reason: stts must account for every sample exactly once: the sum of its run lengths equals the stsz sample_count of the same track. A short stts makes ffmpeg run out of timing entries before the samples do and it pads with a default delta; a long one makes it index past the sample table.

then.equals: a grouping whose implied total sample count equals the stsz sample_count of the same track

dependencies.reason: stsc entries are a run-length description of chunk contents: entry i applies from first_chunk[i] up to first_chunk[i+1]-1, the last entry applies through the final chunk, first_chunk must start at 1 and strictly increase, and samples_per_chunk times the number of chunks it covers must sum to the track's sample_count. Getting this wrong is the single most common cause of ffmpeg reporting a valid container with zero decoded frames.

then.max: the entry_count of the same track's stco or co64

dependencies.reason: Chunk numbers are 1-based and must not exceed the number of chunk offsets declared; a first_chunk beyond the table makes ffmpeg read an offset that does not exist.

then.max: the stsz sample_count of the same track

dependencies.reason: stss lists sync samples by 1-based number in increasing order; values outside the sample range or out of order make ffmpeg's binary search over the sync table miss, which breaks seeking and, for codecs that need a key frame to start, breaks decoding from the beginning.

then.equals: the sum over stts entries of str_stts.sample_count multiplied by str_stts.sample_delta, expressed in mdhd time_scale units

dependencies.reason: The media duration declared in mdhd should equal the total playing time the sample tables imply; ffmpeg uses it to size the timeline and to decide when the stream ends, and a value far shorter than the tables causes it to stop reading samples early.

then.equals: the enclosing track's mdhd duration multiplied by mvhd.time_scale and divided by mdhd.time_scale

dependencies.reason: tkhd duration is expressed in the MOVIE time scale while mdhd duration is in the MEDIA time scale, so the two are related by the ratio of the time scales; the .bt comment at line 782 states the units explicitly.

then.equals: the largest tkhd duration over all tracks, in movie time scale units

dependencies.reason: The movie duration is the longest track; ffmpeg takes it as the container duration for progress reporting and for deciding when to stop demuxing.

then.equals: one more than the largest mp4box.track_id in the file, or 1 when there are no tracks

dependencies.reason: ISO/IEC 14496-12 requires next_track_id to be greater than every track ID in use; a value that collides makes ffmpeg reject subsequently added track IDs as duplicates.

then.equals: the number of samples in the enclosing track fragment or track, i.e. stsz sample_count for a whole-file table or the sum of the trun sample_count values of the enclosing traf

dependencies.reason: senc carries exactly one entry per sample, in sample order; a count that disagrees with the sample table makes the IVs line up with the wrong samples and every CENC decryption after the first mismatch produces garbage that the codec rejects.

then.equals: a split whose per-subsample sum of bytes_of_clear_data plus bytes_of_protected_data equals the size of that sample

dependencies.reason: The subsample split partitions each sample into alternating clear and protected runs; ISO/IEC 23001-7 requires the parts to add up to the sample size exactly, and ffmpeg decrypts only the protected runs, so an over-long split reads past the sample into the next one.

then.equals: tenc default_per_sample_IV_size plus 2 plus 6 times that sample's subsample_count when useSubsampleEncryption is set, otherwise tenc default_per_sample_IV_size

dependencies.reason: Each saiz entry is the byte length of the corresponding senc entry for that sample; ffmpeg uses it to walk the auxiliary information, so a wrong size desynchronises every later sample's IV.

then.equals: the byte offset of each senc box the fragment uses, resolved from the base data offset of the enclosing moof when tfhd base-data-offset-present is clear, or absolute from the start of the file otherwise

dependencies.reason: saio is a list of pointers to sample-auxiliary-information boxes; ffmpeg adds the fragment's base data offset before dereferencing, so the values must be written in the same frame of reference the tfhd flags declare. entry_count must equal the number of senc boxes pointed at, normally one per traf.

then.equals: the track_id of the track this index describes

dependencies.reason: sidx references are attributed to a track by ID; a referenceID that matches no track makes ffmpeg ignore the index, and one that matches the wrong track corrupts that track's seeking.

then.equals: the byte length of the referenced material, OR-ed with 0x80000000 when the reference points at another sidx rather than at media

dependencies.reason: The references of a sidx must tile the referenced bytes contiguously and completely, and the top bit selects index-to-index rather than index-to-media; ffmpeg uses the sizes to compute byte-range seeks, so a wrong size sends every seek to the wrong offset.

then.interpretation: an empty edit that delays the track by duration movie-time units without consuming any media

dependencies.reason: A media_time of -1 marks an empty segment used for audio/video priming or delay; any other value is a 0-based media-time offset that must fall inside the track's media duration, and ffmpeg rejects edits that start beyond the end of the media.

then.equals: the number of sample-entry boxes written inside the same stsd

dependencies.reason: A track needs at least one sample description or ffmpeg has no codec to bind; the count must equal the number of nested boxes actually emitted, because line 667 reads exactly that many.

then.condition: in the trex of the same track, or in the tfhd of the enclosing traf

dependencies.reason: When a trun omits per-sample sizes the sample size comes from the tfhd default, which in turn falls back to the trex default; at least one of the two must be present or the fragment's samples have no length and ffmpeg reports zero-size samples.

structure.subject: ftyp
structure.detail: The first box of the file shall be an ftyp box, and the file shall begin at offset 0 with its 8-byte boxheader (or 16-byte header when size==1).
structure.description: A decoder identifies an ISO base media file by the ftyp brand box at the very start of the file.
structure.generation_note: Emit ftyp as a fixed head element: major_brand, minor_version, then a compatible_brands array bounded by the output_budget below.

structure.subject: mp4box.box at every level, including the top level
structure.detail: Boxes shall tile their enclosing region exactly: no gap between the end of one box and the start of the next, no overlap, and the last top-level box shall end exactly at the end of the file.
structure.description: Every container reads a child header, descends into it, then seeks to box.endOffset before reading the next child, so any byte not covered by a box is never read and any overshoot lands the next header inside a payload.
structure.output_budget: Whole file: keep a running total of bytes emitted and stop adding new top-level boxes when the total would exceed 4 MiB (4194304 bytes). The budget is on the file, never on boxheader.size or on any count field; an individual box may take any legal size up to the remaining budget.
structure.generation_note: Build the box tree, compute each box's size from its already-serialised children, then write sizes top-down. Fill any leftover space with a free box rather than leaving a gap.

structure.subject: moov
structure.detail: Exactly one moov box shall be present in the file, and it shall contain exactly one mvhd.
structure.description: moov is the movie container and mvhd carries the movie time scale, duration and next_track_id that every track is interpreted against; without them the file has no track list.
structure.output_budget: moov is a single instance, so this rule contributes no count of its own; its byte total is the running sum the generator accumulates as it writes the section: mvhd (108 bytes at version 0, 120 at version 1) plus the trak array, whose total is bounded by the 'trak inside moov' budget below, plus mvex, meta, udta and any padding box it chooses to add. The generator picks the movie-header budget first, spends it on tracks, and stops adding tracks when it is reached. The budget is a byte total only - it never caps mp4box.next_track_id, mp4box.track_id or any other field's legal span.
structure.generation_note: Emit moov as a fixed section: mvhd, then a trak array bounded by output_budget, then optionally mvex, meta, udta and padding boxes.

structure.subject: trak inside moov
structure.detail: moov shall contain one or more trak boxes. Each trak shall contain exactly one tkhd, exactly one mdia, at most one edts, at most one tref, and zero or more udta.
structure.description: tkhd binds the track ID and movie timeline while mdia carries the media itself; edts and tref are optional refinements and udta is free metadata.
structure.output_budget: Tracks: keep a running total of the bytes contributed by all trak boxes (their own tables plus their share of mdat) and stop adding tracks when that total would exceed 3.5 MiB (3670016 bytes). Single-track and multi-track files must both be emitted; the budget decides when to stop and never fixes the count.
structure.generation_note: Emit at least one video or audio track first, then add further tracks while the budget allows, varying the handler subtype each time.

structure.subject: mdhd, hdlr and minf inside mdia
structure.detail: Each mdia shall contain exactly one mdhd, exactly one hdlr and exactly one minf.
structure.description: mdhd supplies the media time scale that converts sample deltas into time, hdlr names the handler that decides the stream type, and minf holds the sample tables; all three are needed before any sample can be decoded.
structure.output_budget: This rule fixes the instance count at exactly one each, so it adds no count of its own and carries no independent total: mdhd is 32 bytes (version 0) or 44 (version 1), hdlr is 33 bytes plus the handler name, and minf's own subtree is bounded by the budgets of the rules below it. The running total these contribute is charged to the enclosing trak, whose budget already accounts for the per-track media-box overhead. No field's legal span is narrowed to fit.
structure.generation_note: Fixed head (mdhd, hdlr) followed by the minf subtree.

structure.subject: vmhd, smhd, hmhd, nmhd and gmhd inside minf
structure.detail: Each minf shall contain exactly one media-information header, and the choice shall agree with the enclosing track's hdlr subtype: 'vide' with vmhd, 'soun' with smhd, 'hint' with hmhd, and 'meta', 'text', 'subt', 'sbtl' or 'tmcd' with nmhd or gmhd.
structure.condition: always; which single one is required is decided by the track's hdlr subtype
structure.description: The media header carries the type-specific presentation parameters, and the handler subtype is what selects the stream-type code path in a decoder.
structure.output_budget: Exactly one media-information header per minf, so the choice adds no count and no independent total: vmhd, smhd, hmhd, nmhd and gmhd are all 8 to 20 bytes, and whichever is picked is charged to the enclosing trak's budget. Choosing among the five is a free diversity axis with no size consequence, so the generator may vary it per track without checking any total of its own.
structure.generation_note: Derive the media header from the hdlr subtype already chosen for the track, never the other way round.

structure.subject: dinf and dref inside minf
structure.detail: Each minf shall contain exactly one dinf, and that dinf shall contain exactly one dref whose entry_count equals the number of data-reference entries written inside it.
structure.description: dinf/dref declare where the media data comes from, and a self-contained file needs at least the single url entry with flag 0x000001 set meaning 'the data is in this file'.
structure.output_budget: Data references: keep a running total of dref entry bytes across all tracks and stop adding entries when it would exceed 8 KiB (8192 bytes); entry_count stays free up to that budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit one self-contained url entry for the common case, then vary the reference types while the budget allows.

structure.subject: stbl inside minf
structure.detail: Each minf shall contain exactly one stbl holding the track's sample tables.
structure.description: stbl is the only place a non-fragmented track's sample layout is described, so without it there is nothing to map samples to bytes.
structure.output_budget: Exactly one stbl per minf, so this rule adds no count and no independent total: the stbl box itself is 8 header bytes plus the 8-byte full-box version/flags, and everything inside it is bounded by the budgets of the rules that follow. Its bytes are charged to the enclosing trak's running total, which the generator already checks when it decides how many tracks to emit.
structure.generation_note: Fixed section; its children are covered by the rules that follow.

structure.subject: stsd, stts, stsc, stsz and stco-or-co64 inside stbl
structure.detail: Each stbl shall contain exactly one stsd, exactly one stts, exactly one stsc, exactly one stsz, and exactly one of stco or co64.
structure.description: These five tables are the minimum complete description of a track's samples: what they are, how long each lasts, how they group into chunks, how big each is, and where each chunk starts.
structure.output_budget: Exactly one of each, so this rule fixes five instance counts at one and carries no independent total of its own: the bytes of each table are bounded by the entry-array budgets that follow (str_stts entries, str_stsc entries, the stsz entry_size array, the stco or co64 chunk_offset array, and mp4box.entries inside stsd). The five headers contribute 40 bytes to the enclosing stbl, which is charged to the trak total. Because the counts are fixed at one here, the only size freedom is inside the arrays, and no array's entry-count field is narrowed - the generator picks a media-byte budget first and lets every array length fall out of it.
structure.generation_note: Write the media samples first, derive every table from that sample list, then serialise the tables and fill the chunk offsets in afterwards.

structure.subject: stco versus co64 inside stbl
structure.detail: stco and co64 shall not both appear in the same stbl.
structure.description: They are two encodings of the same chunk-offset table, and a decoder applies whichever it read last, silently discarding the other.
structure.generation_note: Choose co64 when any chunk offset exceeds 0xFFFFFFFF; otherwise choose freely between the two, but never emit both.

structure.subject: optional refinement boxes inside stbl: ctts, cslg, sdtp, sbgp, sgpd, subs, padb
structure.detail: stbl may additionally contain one each of ctts, cslg, sdtp, sbgp, sgpd, subs and padb, alongside the stss, saio and saiz boxes the template does name; the one-each figure is the specification's own cardinality, not a generator limit, and the byte size of each table is governed by the output_budget below rather than by any entry-count cap.

structure.description: These are independent optional refinement tables, so omitting one only removes the information it carries while duplicating one makes a decoder apply whichever copy it read last.
structure.output_budget: Total bytes for the whole optional-refinement group per track is the free parameter and is what the generator may vary; choose it as a fraction of the enclosing stbl size, then let the number of records in each individual table be whatever that budget and the fixed sample list imply. Never bound a single table's record count directly: a track with thousands of samples may need a ctts or subs with thousands of records, and the budget must be allowed to grow with the sample count so no valid table is truncated.
structure.generation_note: Decide per track which optional tables to include, then derive each table from the already-fixed sample list; the template will skip them cleanly either way, so their presence costs nothing structurally.

structure.subject: mdat
structure.detail: At least one mdat shall be present whenever any track has samples, and every byte range that a sample table or a trun data offset points at shall lie inside some mdat.
structure.description: mdat is the only container for media payload, so anything it does not hold is unreachable by the tables.
structure.output_budget: Media payload: keep a running total of bytes written into all mdat boxes and stop adding samples when that total would exceed 3 MiB (3145728 bytes). The sample count, the per-sample size and the number of mdat boxes all stay free; only the running byte total gates further samples.

structure.subject: mdat payload
structure.detail: The samples of one track shall occupy contiguous, non-overlapping byte ranges in the order the tables describe them; different tracks may interleave or share regions.
structure.description: Two samples of the same track pointing at the same bytes decode the same access unit twice, and a gap makes a decoder read unrelated bytes as an access unit.
structure.output_budget: The total number of media-sample bytes across the whole file is the running total the generator checks and stops at; it is the dominant term in file size, so pick it first and let every per-sample size be chosen inside it. It is a byte total only - never a cap on mp4box.sample_count, mp4box.entry_size or str_stts.sample_count, whose legal spans stay full width. A budget of a few tens of kilobytes already exercises the chunk-offset, stsc-grouping and trun-offset arithmetic, and the same budget may be spent as many small samples or few large ones.
structure.generation_note: Lay samples out sequentially from the mdat data start, optionally interleaving tracks at chunk granularity.

structure.subject: moof
structure.detail: No moof box shall appear before the moov box.

structure.generation_note: Always emit ftyp, then moov (including mvex), then the fragment sequence.

structure.subject: moof and traf

structure.description: mvex declares the movie fragmented and lists the per-track defaults, mfhd numbers the fragments, and each traf binds one track's runs to a trex.
structure.output_budget: Fragments: keep a running total of all moof bytes plus the mdat bytes they reference and stop adding fragments when it would exceed 3 MiB (3145728 bytes). The number of fragments, the number of traf boxes per moof and the number of trun boxes per traf all stay free within that budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit mfhd with a strictly increasing sequence_number, then one traf per active track, then one or more trun per traf, then the mdat for that fragment.

structure.subject: mfra, tfra and mfro
structure.detail: If mfra is present it shall be the last box of the file, it shall contain one tfra per fragmented track, and mfro shall be the last box inside it.
structure.condition: the template names none of these three types, so they all reach the default branch at line 798 and are consumed as opaque bytes; the ordering requirement is from the spec and from how a reader finds the box

structure.generation_note: Emit one tfra per fragmented track, then mfro carrying the byte size of the whole mfra box, then nothing after mfra.

structure.subject: sinf, frma, schm, schi and tenc

structure.subject: str_stts entries inside stts
structure.detail: stts holds entry_count run-length records and entry_count shall equal the number written; the records shall cover every sample of the track exactly once.
structure.description: entry_count is a repeat bound driven purely by how many distinct durations the generator chooses to use, so it is the output budget and not a value cap that decides how large it gets.
structure.output_budget: Timing table: keep a running total of stts entry bytes (8 bytes each) across all tracks and stop adding entries when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file; entry_count and str_stts.sample_count stay free up to that budget.
