structure.subject: str_stsc entries inside stsc
structure.detail: stsc holds entry_count chunk-mapping records; the first record's first_chunk shall be 1 and first_chunk shall strictly increase across records.
structure.description: The record count follows from the chunk layout the generator picked, and a layout with many distinct samples_per_chunk values is more interesting to a decoder than one uniform value.
structure.output_budget: Chunk-mapping table: keep a running total of stsc entry bytes (12 bytes each) across all tracks and stop adding entries when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Fix the chunk grouping, then emit one record at each point where samples_per_chunk changes.

structure.subject: mp4box.entry_size array inside stsz
structure.detail: When stsz sample_size is 0, entry_size holds exactly sample_count uint32 lengths, one per sample, in sample order.
structure.description: This is the per-sample length array and its length is set by the number of media samples the generator produced, which is a diversity axis rather than a constant.
structure.output_budget: Size table: keep a running total of stsz entry bytes (4 bytes each) across all tracks and stop adding samples when it would exceed 128 KiB (131072 bytes) per file. Equivalently the generator stops adding samples when the running mdat byte total hits its own budget; sample_count itself is never capped.
structure.generation_note: Derive every entry from the encoded access unit's real byte length; never invent a length and then pad the sample to fit it.

structure.subject: mp4box.chunk_offset array inside stco or co64
structure.detail: stco holds entry_count uint32 offsets and co64 holds entry_count uint64 offsets, one per chunk of the track, in chunk order.
structure.description: The array length equals the number of chunks, which is decided by the interleaving the generator chose.
structure.output_budget: Chunk-offset table: keep a running total of chunk-offset bytes across all tracks and stop adding chunks when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Lay the samples out, record the file offset where each chunk begins, then write the array; recompute the offsets after the moov size is known, since moov's own length shifts mdat.

structure.subject: mp4box.sample_number array inside stss
structure.detail: stss holds entry_count sample numbers in strictly increasing order, each within 1..stsz sample_count; entry_count of 0 means every sample is a sync sample.
structure.description: The sync-sample list is what drives seeking, and both a sparse list and an empty one exercise different decoder paths.
structure.output_budget: Sync-sample table: keep a running total of stss entry bytes (4 bytes each) across all tracks and stop adding entries when it would exceed 32 KiB (32768 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Emit the numbers of the access units that are really key frames, sorted; omit stss entirely for all-intra material.

structure.subject: composition-offset records inside ctts
structure.detail: ctts holds entry_count run-length records, each a sample_count and a sample_offset shared by that many samples; entry_count of 0 means presentation order equals decode order, and version 1 makes sample_offset a signed int32 so negative offsets are expressible.
structure.condition: ctts is not one of the types the template's stbl switch names, so it reaches the default branch at line 798 and is consumed as opaque bytes; the field layout is from ISO/IEC 14496-12 subclause 8.6.1.3
structure.description: The record count follows from how many distinct composition offsets the generator's frame reordering produces, and B-frame material needs it while all-intra material does not.
structure.output_budget: Composition-offset table: keep a running total of ctts record bytes (8 bytes each) across all tracks and stop adding records when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Derive each record from the B-frame reordering pattern, run-length-encode equal offsets, and use version 1 whenever any offset is negative.

structure.subject: mp4box.entries inside stsd
structure.detail: stsd holds entry_count complete sample-entry boxes, each a self-describing mp4box with its own codec configuration children.
structure.description: Multiple sample descriptions in one track is legal and drives the decoder through a different codec-initialisation path per entry.
structure.output_budget: Sample descriptions: keep a running total of stsd entry bytes across all tracks and stop adding entries when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file; entry_count stays free up to that budget and shall never be pinned at 1.
structure.generation_note: Build each entry as a full box: the codec FourCC, the fixed visual or audio fields, then the configuration children (avcC, hvcC, esds, sinf) and finally the optional pasp, colr, btrt and clap.

structure.subject: compatible_brand entries inside ftyp
structure.detail: ftyp carries major_brand, minor_version and then a list of compatible brands that runs until the box's content region is exhausted; the number of brands is whatever the generator writes.
structure.description: The brand list is read by a size-driven loop, so its length is a pure formatting choice that changes which compatibility profiles a decoder believes the file claims.
structure.output_budget: Brand list: keep a running total of compatible-brand bytes (4 bytes each) and stop adding brands when it would exceed 256 bytes.
structure.generation_note: Always include major_brand in the list, then add further brands for the profiles the generator wants a decoder to accept.

structure.subject: elst_entry records inside elst
structure.detail: elst holds num_entries edit records; num_entries of 0 is legal and means the whole media is played, and any positive value shall have that many records written.
structure.description: The edit list drives trimming, delay and playback-rate handling, and the empty list is a distinct decoder path from a populated one.
structure.output_budget: Edit lists: keep a running total of elst entry bytes across all tracks and stop adding entries when it would exceed 8 KiB (8192 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Emit 0 entries for a pass-through track, otherwise one record per edit segment with media_time -1 for empty segments.

structure.subject: str_sidx references inside sidx
structure.detail: sidx holds reference_count references, each 12 bytes, and the referenced regions shall follow one another without gaps.
structure.description: The reference count follows from how the generator split the timeline into indexed segments, and both a single whole-file index and a fine-grained per-fragment index occur in real streams.
structure.output_budget: Segment index: keep a running total of sidx reference bytes (12 bytes each) across the file and stop adding references when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes).
structure.generation_note: Write the referenced material first, record each segment's byte length and subsegment duration, then emit the references.

structure.subject: mp4box.KID entries inside pssh
structure.detail: pssh version 1 or later holds KID_count 16-byte key IDs followed by DataSize bytes of system-specific data; version 0 holds no key IDs.
structure.description: The key-ID count is a repeat bound that changes how a DRM-aware decoder walks the box, and the data blob after it is opaque and free.
structure.output_budget: Key IDs: keep a running total of pssh bytes across all pssh boxes and stop adding key IDs or data when it would exceed 8 KiB (8192 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Emit one 16-byte KID per key the track uses, then DataSize and the system-specific payload; repeat the whole pssh box for each DRM system UUID the generator wants to advertise.

structure.subject: senc per-sample entries and their subsample records
structure.detail: senc holds sample_count entries; each entry is the per-sample IV followed by subsample_count records of bytes_of_clear_data and bytes_of_protected_data when the useSubsampleEncryption flag is set.
structure.description: Both the whole-sample and the subsample encryption shape are real and take different decryption paths, and the sample count is fixed by the fragment's sample list rather than chosen for size.
structure.output_budget: Encryption auxiliary information: keep a running total of senc bytes across all senc boxes and stop adding samples when it would exceed 128 KiB (131072 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Fix the sample list and IV size first, then write one entry per sample; derive saiz from the entry lengths and saio from the senc box offsets.

structure.subject: saio offsets and saiz sizes
structure.detail: saio holds entry_count offsets, one per referenced auxiliary-information box, and saiz holds a default_sample_info_size plus one size byte per sample; saiz sample_count shall equal the track's sample count.
structure.description: These two boxes are pointer and length tables for senc, so their lengths are determined by the encryption layout the generator already chose.
structure.output_budget: Auxiliary-information pointers: keep a running total of saio and saiz bytes across all fragments and stop adding entries when it would exceed 128 KiB (131072 bytes) per file.
structure.generation_note: Write senc first, then record its offset relative to the moof base and each entry's byte length, then emit saio and saiz from those recordings.

structure.subject: free, skip, wide and every other box type the template does not name
structure.detail: Any number of padding boxes may appear at any level; each shall have a size of at least its own header length, and together they shall keep the parent's content region exactly tiled.
structure.condition: free is named in the template's BoxComment registry at line 209 but has no case in the switch, so it and skip, wide and every other unrecognised FourCC all reach 'default: FSkip(contentsize)' at lines 798-799
structure.description: Padding is how the generator positions mdat and absorbs the change in moov's length once the tables are known, without touching a single media byte.
structure.output_budget: Padding: keep a running total of padding bytes and stop adding padding boxes when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file; individual box sizes stay free up to the remaining budget.
structure.generation_note: Compute the final moov length, then insert one free box between moov and mdat of exactly the slack needed so the chunk offsets already written stay correct.

structure.subject: default branch of the mp4box switch: any boxheader.type with no case
structure.detail: A box whose type has no case in the switch is still a well-formed box: its header is read normally, its contentsize bytes are skipped, and the enclosing container loop continues from box.endOffset. Any FourCC may therefore appear anywhere a container allows children.
structure.description: This is the template's escape hatch and a real demuxer's too, so an unknown box type is a free structural axis rather than an error, as long as its size field is honest.
structure.output_budget: Unknown boxes: keep a running total of bytes spent on boxes the template skips and stop adding them when it would exceed 64 KiB (65536 bytes) per file; the number and size of individual unknown boxes stay free up to that budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit spec-defined boxes the template does not implement (ctts, sdtp, sbgp, sgpd, subs, tfdt, mfra, tfra, mfro, meta and the codec configuration children avcC, hvcC and esds) with well-formed content: a real decoder parses them even though this template skips them.

structure.subject: children of stbl, minf, trak, moov, moof, traf and every other container
structure.detail: The format imposes no order on the children of a container except where a rule above says so (mfhd first in moof, mfro last in mfra); the container loops read whatever boxes appear until the parent's content region is exhausted.
structure.description: Order freedom is a real diversity axis, because a decoder that caches tables in parse order sees a different state when stco precedes stsz than when it follows.
structure.output_budget: This ordering rule adds no bytes of its own, so it carries no independent total: the bytes of the children it reorders are already bounded by the budget of the enclosing container (trak inside moov, mp4box.entries inside stsd, the optional-refinement group inside stbl, and the free/unknown-box group). Reordering is free, so the generator should permute child order across files without any size cost and without touching a single field's legal span.
structure.generation_note: Vary the child order across generated files, but always write the chunk offsets after the sizes are known and fix the offsets up in a second pass.

structure.subject: trex inside mvex
structure.detail: Every track that appears in a moof shall have exactly one trex in moov's mvex whose trackID equals that track's tkhd track_id.
structure.description: trex supplies the per-track fragment defaults that tfhd and trun fall back on, so a fragment for an undeclared track has no defaults and contributes no samples.
structure.output_budget: mvex repeats one trex per track, so the running total is bounded by the track count already fixed by the 'trak inside moov' budget: 24 bytes of trex per declared track, plus the mvex and mvhd headers. The generator checks the accumulated moov size against that budget and stops adding tracks when it is reached. The number of tracks is not capped by a count anywhere - it falls out of the moov byte budget - and no trex field's legal span is narrowed to save space.
structure.generation_note: Emit one trex per track immediately after mvhd inside mvex, using the same track_id values the tkhd boxes already declared.

diversity_axes.why: The size word decides how many bytes every following box occupies and therefore where every later box header lands; it is the single field that turns a box tree into a byte layout.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Size 1 selects the 16-byte header with a uint64 largesize, size 0 selects 'extends to end of container or file', and any other value selects the ordinary 8-byte header. A demuxer walks the whole file through this field, so small boxes, page-sized boxes and gigabyte-sized boxes exercise different offset arithmetic and different seek paths.

diversity_axes.why: It is the length of the sample list, and every other table in the track is derived from it; pinning it at any particular value would collapse the whole track to one shape.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A one-sample file, a file with a handful of samples and a file with tens of thousands take different paths through the sample-table build, the interleave decision, the seek-index construction and the packet queue; the count also decides whether stts, stsc and stco need more than one run-length record.

diversity_axes.why: It selects between the two stsz encodings: a uniform size for every sample, or zero meaning 'read the per-sample array'. Both are real and both are common.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Non-zero lets a demuxer compute any sample's offset by multiplication without touching an array; zero forces it to walk entry_size. The two paths differ in allocation, in bounds checking and in how a truncated table is handled.

diversity_axes.why: The per-sample length array; its values are the real byte lengths of the encoded access units and must be derived from the payload, never chosen to suit a size target.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Uniform lengths, wildly varying lengths (typical of B-frame video where reference frames are an order of magnitude larger) and very large single samples each drive different buffer-growth and read-ahead behaviour in a demuxer.

diversity_axes.why: In trex and tfhd it is the fallback sample length for every sample in a fragment that does not carry its own trun size; it is a free choice that changes whether trun needs the sample-size flag at all.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A default of zero with per-sample trun sizes, a non-zero default with the trun size flag clear, and a mixture all reach different branches of the fragment-sample construction code.

diversity_axes.why: It selects between whole-sample encryption and subsample encryption, and its value is the number of clear/protected runs inside one sample, which is a property of the codec bitstream being protected.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero subsamples means the whole sample after the IV is ciphertext; two means a clear NAL header run followed by a protected run, which is what CENC in practice does for H.264 and HEVC; many subsamples means a NAL-by-NAL split. A CENC decryptor takes a different code path per case and only the subsample path exercises the partial-decrypt logic.

diversity_axes.why: The length of each clear run inside an encrypted sample; it must equal the real number of unencrypted bytes the generator wrote, which is dictated by the codec framing.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A zero clear run sends the whole sample to the cipher; a non-zero run makes the decryptor copy the prefix straight through and decrypt only the remainder, and the boundary lands at different points in the NAL structure depending on the value.

diversity_axes.why: The length of each encrypted run; together with bytes_of_clear_data it must sum to the sample's real byte length, so it is derived from the payload and never set independently.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Determines how many bytes the CENC decryptor feeds to the block cipher and therefore which cipher mode boundaries (cbc1 versus cens versus cbcs subsample patterns) are exercised; a zero protected run means an entirely clear sample inside an encrypted track.

diversity_axes.why: It is the repeat bound for stsd sample entries and for every counted table array (stts, stsc, stco, co64, stss, ctts, saio); it counts real records, so capping it would remove structure rather than size.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: entry_count 1 in stsd means a single codec for the track, while 2 or more makes a demuxer build several codec contexts and resolve sample_description_index per chunk. In the sample tables, 1 means a single run-length record covering everything and many means a decoder walking a real table with binary search.

diversity_axes.why: The track's presentation width as a 16.16 fixed-point fp32 in tkhd; it is independent of the coded width in the sample entry and of the display aspect ratio, so it is a free scaling axis.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Values equal to the coded size, values that scale it up or down, and fractional values all reach the track-geometry and aspect-ratio computation; a fractional or zero width takes a different normalisation path than an integral one.

diversity_axes.why: The track's presentation height, the vertical counterpart of width and equally free for the same reasons.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Together with width it decides whether a demuxer applies an anamorphic stretch, a straight copy or a rejection path for degenerate geometry; tall, wide, square and zero-height tracks all behave differently.

diversity_axes.why: The byte length of the sample-description payload region; the live stsd path reads entry_count nested boxes out of exactly this many bytes, so the two must agree and the value comes from the entries that were built.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A small content region holding one compact audio entry, a large one holding a video entry with several configuration children, and one holding multiple entries all take different amounts of the sample-description parse loop and different allocation paths.

diversity_axes.why: The length of the pssh system-specific data blob that follows it; the blob is opaque to the container so its length is a free axis, and the field is only required to match what was written.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means an empty payload box, which a DRM-aware reader still honours as a system declaration; a large blob exercises the allocation and copy path and, for real systems, the parsing of the embedded licence or key information.

diversity_axes.why: The 16-byte UUID naming the DRM system a pssh box belongs to; it is data, not a count, and every distinct value routes a reader to a different protection-system handler.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The well-known UUIDs (Widevine, PlayReady, FairPlay, ClearKey and the common-encryption signalling UUID) each select a different code path in a DRM-aware demuxer, while an unrecognised UUID takes the generic 'store and pass through' path; all of them are legal to emit.

diversity_axes.why: The run length of one timing record; it is how many consecutive samples share a duration, and it is a property of the media the generator decided to write.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: One record covering the whole track, one record per sample, and a handful of long records with short exceptions each produce a different timestamp table shape, which changes how a demuxer computes per-sample PTS and how it interpolates when seeking.

diversity_axes.why: The duration of each sample in the run, in media time scale units; combined with mdhd time_scale it sets the whole track's playing rate, and it is entirely free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A constant delta gives constant-frame-rate material, alternating deltas give variable-frame-rate material, and a zero delta gives a run of samples sharing one timestamp; each takes a different path through PTS computation and through any duplicate-frame detection.

diversity_axes.why: How many samples sit in each chunk of a run; it is the interleaving granularity the generator chose and it directly shapes the chunk-offset table.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: One sample per chunk gives maximum interleaving and a long offset table, many samples per chunk gives few large reads, and a mixture across records forces a demuxer to walk a real mapping table rather than assume a constant. Chunked reads, buffer reuse and seek granularity all differ.

diversity_axes.why: The chunk number at which a mapping record starts applying; the set of values encodes the chunk layout and must stay as free as the layout itself.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A single record starting at 1 means every chunk is identical, while records starting at 1, 2, 100 and so on mean the layout changes part-way through the file and a demuxer has to interpolate between records to find any given chunk's contents.

diversity_axes.why: The edit-list record count in elst; zero, one and many are all legal and each describes a different playback intent.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero entries means play the whole media unchanged and skips the edit machinery entirely, one entry means a simple trim or delay, and several entries mean a real composition of segments that a demuxer has to splice, including the empty-edit case where media_time is -1.

diversity_axes.why: The number of references in a sidx; it is how finely the generator chose to index the timeline and is bounded only by the output budget.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: One reference covering everything gives a coarse index, many references give fine-grained byte-range seeking, and a reference whose top bit is set points at another sidx rather than at media, which makes a reader build a two-level index instead of a flat one.

diversity_axes.why: The number of 16-byte key IDs a pssh box declares; a track may be licensed under several keys and the count is a free property of the protection signalling.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero key IDs (version 0), one, and several each change how a DRM-aware reader matches the box against a licence and how it correlates the pssh with the tenc default_KID.

diversity_axes.why: The fragment number in mfhd; a stream may have any number of fragments and the number is only required to increase, so the count of fragments is a free axis governed by the output budget.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A single-fragment file, a file with a handful of fragments and a long-running fragmented stream exercise different state in a demuxer: fragment detection, gap detection for missing fragments, and the incremental append path that grows the track as each moof arrives.

diversity_axes.why: The FullBox version byte selects between two field widths in mvhd, mdhd, tkhd, elst, saio, sidx, mehd and trun; both versions are legal in every one of those boxes and a generator that always emits 0 loses half the parsing paths.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Version 0 reads 32-bit times, durations and offsets; version 1 reads 64-bit ones and, in trun, a signed composition offset. The two versions also differ in whether negative values are expressible at all, so version 1 reaches code that version 0 cannot.

diversity_axes.why: The 24-bit FullBox flags word is a bank of structure-selecting switches in tfhd, trun, saio, saiz, senc, dref and tkhd; which bits are set decides which following members exist at all.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each bit combination produces a different record layout, so the per-sample loop in trun, the auxiliary-type prefix in saio/saiz and the subsample records in senc are each reached only for particular flag values. Emitting the full range of combinations walks every branch.

diversity_axes.why: Every FourCC in the format is data, and the value chosen for hdlr type and subtype, for major_brand and compatible brands, for a sample entry and for a codec configuration child selects the entire downstream code path.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: hdlr subtype 'vide' builds a video stream, 'soun' an audio stream, 'hint' an RTP hint stream, 'text'/'subt'/'sbtl' a subtitle stream; each has its own media header, its own sample-entry layout and its own parser. The sample-entry FourCC then selects which codec is instantiated.

diversity_axes.why: The primary brand declares which profile of the format the file claims to follow, and it is free data rather than a count.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 'isom', 'iso2', 'mp41', 'mp42', 'M4V ', 'M4A ', 'F4V ' and 'qt  ' each make a demuxer apply a different compatibility profile, and 'qt  ' in particular switches on the QuickTime-only atom set and the QuickTime language, graphics-mode and matrix interpretations.

diversity_axes.why: Each compatible brand is an independent FourCC in a size-driven list; the number and the identities of the brands are both free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A reader checks the list to decide whether it can handle the file at all, and each additional brand may enable an optional feature path (fragmentation, negative composition offsets, timed text). An empty or minimal list versus a long one changes which feature probes succeed.

diversity_axes.why: The 16-bit language field is free data with two distinct encodings packed into one field, and both are legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A value below 0x400 is a QuickTime macintosh language code looked up in an enum; a value at or above 0x400 is three 5-bit ISO-639-2/T characters each stored as character minus 0x60. The two encodings take completely different decode paths and produce different language metadata.

diversity_axes.why: The number of media or movie time units per second; it is a free choice that rescales every duration and timestamp in the file without changing a single sample byte.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A timescale equal to the frame rate gives integer deltas of 1, a timescale of 90000 (the MPEG system clock) gives large deltas, and a high timescale exercises the 64-bit accumulation paths a demuxer uses to avoid rounding. Fractional-second durations only exist at certain timescales.

diversity_axes.why: The declared length of the media, the track or the movie; it is derived from the sample tables and the timescale, and the generator must derive it from them rather than pin it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A duration shorter than the tables imply makes a demuxer stop early, a longer one makes it pad with silence or frozen frames, and an exact one takes the normal path. Zero duration is legal for a live or unknown-length stream and selects yet another path.

diversity_axes.why: The identifier that binds tkhd, trex, tfhd, tref and sidx together; it is free data and any set of distinct values is legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Dense IDs starting at 1, sparse IDs, and large IDs near 0xFFFFFFFF each take a different path through the track lookup, and fragmented output additionally exercises the trex-to-tfhd matching. Re-using an ID across tracks makes a demuxer reject the duplicate, which is itself a path worth reaching.

diversity_axes.why: Creation and modification timestamps are pure metadata with no effect on the media, and the seconds-since-1904 epoch encoding means the legal values span more than a century.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero (the conventional 'unknown' value), a 1904 epoch value, a modern UTC value and a value that overflows into 64-bit territory at version 1 all decode differently, and only the large values exercise the wide-time arithmetic.

diversity_axes.why: The QuickTime transfer-mode selector in vmhd and gmhd; it is an enumerated but wide-open choice that changes how the video is composited, not how it is decoded.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Mode 0 (srcCopy) is the normal path; the other QuickTime transfer modes select dithering, blending and transparency handling in a QuickTime-aware renderer, and an out-of-range value takes the fall-back-to-copy path.

diversity_axes.why: The transformation matrix in mvhd and tkhd is nine free 16.16 or 2.30 fixed-point values that describe rotation, scaling and translation of the track; none of them is a count and all of them are legal at any value.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The identity matrix is the pass-through path; a 90, 180 or 270 degree rotation makes a demuxer set a display-matrix side-data entry and swap width and height; a scaling matrix makes it recompute the presentation geometry; a singular or degenerate matrix takes the rejection path.

diversity_axes.why: The single track-enabled bit decides whether the track participates in playback; both values are legal and meaningful, and the other flag bits add preview, poster and movie participation.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: An enabled track is demuxed and decoded normally; a disabled track is still parsed but excluded from the presentation, which is a distinct branch in any demuxer that honours the flag. The track_in_preview and track_in_poster bits select additional QuickTime-only paths.

diversity_axes.why: The compositing layer in tkhd is a free int16 that orders tracks front to back; negative, zero and positive values are all legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Layer 0 is the default single-plane path; distinct layers make a renderer composite in order, and equal layers leave the order undefined, which is itself a branch a QuickTime-aware reader handles.

diversity_axes.why: The alternate-group identifier that marks tracks as interchangeable variants of one another; it is free data and grouping is optional.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Group 0 means the track stands alone; a shared non-zero group across tracks makes a player treat them as switchable alternatives (different languages or bitrates) and select one, which is a different code path from playing all tracks.

diversity_axes.why: The original-format FourCC in frma; it is data naming the underlying codec of an encrypted entry and every legal codec FourCC is a valid value.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: It is the only place a demuxer learns what to instantiate after decryption, so each distinct value selects a different codec parser and a different bitstream validation path once the samples are clear.

diversity_axes.why: The FourCC naming the protection scheme in schm; it selects the entire encryption interpretation of the track and every legal scheme is a distinct choice.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 'cenc' means AES-128 counter mode with per-sample IVs, 'cbc1' AES-128 CBC, 'cens' and 'cbcs' their pattern-encrypted variants, and each makes the decryptor apply a different cipher, IV derivation and subsample handling; scheme_version then selects the pattern fields.

diversity_axes.why: The 16-byte default key identifier in tenc; it is opaque key material with no count and no legal-value restriction from the container's point of view.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A zero KID means the key must come from elsewhere, a real KID makes a DRM-aware reader attempt licence lookup and correlation with the pssh entries, and distinct KIDs across tracks make the reader handle per-track key selection.

diversity_axes.why: The initialisation vector for one encrypted sample; it is cryptographically random data and any value is legal and expected.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: All-zero IVs, sequential IVs and random IVs each work but exercise different IV handling, and IV reuse across samples is a security property a well-behaved reader may detect and report; the field is the only per-sample crypto input in senc.

diversity_axes.why: The opaque system-specific payload of a pssh box; its contents are defined by the DRM system named in systemID, so from the container's view every byte is free data.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: An empty blob, a small structured record and a large licence manifest each take a different path in a DRM-aware reader, and only the reader for the matching systemID interprets the bytes at all.

diversity_axes.why: The 16-byte element of the saiz and pssh KID arrays; it is opaque data repeated per element, and the number of elements is governed by the output budget rather than by any count cap.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: In saiz each entry is an auxiliary-data length whose value decides whether the following saio/senc records are reached at all; in pssh each entry is a key identifier that a DRM reader matches against the track's default_KID.

diversity_axes.why: The trailing region of hdlr after the FourCC and flag fields; its length is computed as contentsize minus what was already read, so it is whatever the generator chose to write there.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: An empty tail, a QuickTime name string and an MPEG-4 component-name string each take a different metadata path, and the QuickTime interpretation additionally expects reserved fields that the MPEG interpretation does not.

diversity_axes.why: The secondary version number in ftyp; it is free metadata that refines the brand declaration and has no structural effect.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the common case and skips version-gated feature checks; a non-zero value may unlock profile-specific behaviour in a strict reader, and it is the only version signal besides the brand list.

diversity_axes.why: In trun it is the byte offset of the first sample of the run relative to the fragment's base-data position; it is derived from the fragment layout, so it must stay free to follow the payload and the preceding boxes.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero with base_data_offset present, a positive offset measured from moof, and offsets spanning multiple mdat boxes each select a different addressing path in the fragment reader; the data_offset flag bit is what makes the field exist at all.

diversity_axes.why: The sync-sample numbers in stss; the set of keyframe positions is a property of the encoded video and every subset of the sample range is legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A single entry, one entry per sample, a sparse set (long-GOP video) and an absent stss box entirely (every sample is a sync sample) each take a different seek path: with stss a demuxer must snap the seek target backwards to the nearest listed sample, without it any sample is seekable.

diversity_axes.why: The per-chunk pointer into the stsd entry list; it is free within the range of declared entries and it is what makes multi-codec tracks possible.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A constant 1 means every chunk uses the first sample entry and the index is never consulted; varying indices make a demuxer switch codec context per chunk, a rarely exercised but fully legal path.

diversity_axes.why: The raw int16 behind every 8.8 fixed-point field (tkhd and smhd volume, balance); the whole int16 range is legal and the wrapper struct exists only to give the value a decimal reading.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero, 0x0100 (unity), values above unity, and negative values each take a different normalisation and clipping path in a player that applies gain or pan, and the negative and overflow cases reach saturation code that unity never does.

diversity_axes.why: The raw int32 behind every 16.16 fixed-point field (matrix scale and shear terms, preferred_rate); all 2^32 patterns are legal because the field is defined purely by its scaling.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0x00010000 (unity), 0 (degenerate axis), negative values (flip or rotation past 90 degrees), and very large values each drive different geometry normalisation, and only the non-unity and negative cases exercise the transform-multiplication path rather than the identity shortcut.

diversity_axes.why: The raw int32 behind the 2.30 homogeneous row of the matrix; the encoding differs from fp32 so the same bit pattern means something else, and every value is legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The canonical 0x40000000 for w and 0 for u and v give the identity homogeneous row; any other value makes a renderer apply a projective transform, which is a distinct path from the affine one and is rarely reached in practice.

diversity_axes.why: The vertical-shear coefficient (row 1, column 2) of the transformation matrix; free data, and non-zero values are what make a rotation possible at all.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero keeps the transform axis-aligned and lets a demuxer skip the shear computation; a non-zero value forces the full 3x3 transform and, at the standard rotation constants, produces the 90/180/270 degree display-matrix side data a player uses to rotate the video.

diversity_axes.why: The horizontal-shear coefficient (row 2, column 1); the counterpart of matrix.b and equally free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero with non-zero b gives a pure rotation or flip; non-zero with b zero gives a skew; both non-zero gives a general affine map. Each combination reaches different code in the transform application and in the display-orientation detection.

diversity_axes.why: The vertical-scale coefficient (row 2, column 2); free data whose value sets the track's vertical scaling independently of the height field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Unity means no vertical scaling and the presentation height equals the track height; other values make a renderer recompute the output rectangle, and a negative value flips the image vertically, which is a path no positive value can reach.

diversity_axes.why: The horizontal homogeneous coefficient (row 1, column 3) in 2.30 encoding; free data, and non-zero values turn the affine transform into a projective one.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the affine case every player fast-paths; non-zero forces perspective division per pixel, a code path almost never exercised by real files and therefore high-value for coverage.

diversity_axes.why: The vertical homogeneous coefficient (row 2, column 3); free data with the same projective significance as matrix.u.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero keeps the transform affine; non-zero selects the perspective path and, at extreme values, the degenerate-case handling where the divisor approaches zero.

diversity_axes.why: The horizontal translation coefficient (row 3, column 1) in 16.16 encoding; free data that positions the track in the composition plane.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero places the track at the origin and takes the no-offset fast path; non-zero makes a compositor apply a translation and can move the track partially or wholly off-canvas, which reaches clipping code that a zero offset never does.

diversity_axes.why: The vertical translation coefficient (row 3, column 2); free data and the vertical counterpart of matrix.x.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero versus non-zero selects whether the composition path applies a vertical offset, and negative values place the track above the origin, which is a distinct clipping case.

diversity_axes.why: The homogeneous scale coefficient (row 3, column 3) in 2.30 encoding; free data whose canonical value is 1.0 but which is not required to be.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0x40000000 makes the divisor 1 and skips the division entirely; any other value forces a per-point divide and, near zero, the singular-matrix rejection path. Both are legal to emit.

diversity_axes.why: The red channel of the vmhd opcolor triple; a free uint16 that is operand data for the transfer mode, not a count or a length.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the normal black operand; other values only matter when graphics_mode selects a blending or dithering transfer, in which case the renderer combines the operand with the source and reaches per-mode arithmetic that mode 0 skips.

diversity_axes.why: The green channel of the opcolor triple; free data for the same reason as red.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Non-grey operands make a QuickTime-aware renderer take the colour-aware blending path rather than the luminance-only one, and equal or unequal channel values select different dither tables.

diversity_axes.why: The blue channel of the opcolor triple; free data for the same reason as red and green.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Completes the operand colour; a saturated primary versus black versus mid-grey each reach different blending outcomes in the transfer-mode code.

diversity_axes.why: The vmhd instance of the qtopcolor triple, declared as a 6-byte struct; it is operand colour data with no count, length or legal-value restriction.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Read together with graphics_mode, so the same value ranges reach the blending, dithering and transparency paths only when a non-copy transfer mode is selected; with mode 0 the bytes are parsed and ignored, which is itself a path.

diversity_axes.why: The 36-byte matrix instance in mvhd and tkhd, declared as a struct of nine fixed-point values; it is pure geometry data and every combination of its nine fields is legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: An identity matrix takes the pass-through path in every renderer; a rotation matrix produces display-matrix side data and swaps the presentation axes; a scaled or translated matrix forces the full affine composition; a singular matrix reaches the rejection path. Because it is one struct instance, pinning it would remove all of those at once.

diversity_axes.why: The length of one edit-list segment in movie timescale units; it is a duration the generator chooses to express, not a count of anything, and zero is legal (meaning 'to the end of the media').
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero, a duration equal to the media, a duration shorter than the media (a trim) and one longer than the media (a freeze or pad) each make a demuxer build a different output timeline, and only the non-trivial cases reach the splice and pad logic.

diversity_axes.why: The media-time at which an edit segment starts; the full uint32 range is legal and 0xFFFFFFFF is the special 'empty edit' marker, so the field carries both data and a sentinel.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero starts at the beginning of the media and skips the offset arithmetic; a positive value makes a demuxer drop or delay the head of the track (how audio priming is compensated); 0xFFFFFFFF inserts an empty edit that shifts the track on the movie timeline without playing anything, which is a completely separate branch.

diversity_axes.why: The playback rate of one edit segment as an fp32 (16.16); any value is legal and it is the only field in the format that expresses non-unity playback speed.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 1.0 (0x00010000) plays normally and takes the fast path; other values make a player resample or drop-and-repeat frames, and a zero or negative rate reaches the reverse-playback or stall handling that unity never exercises.

diversity_axes.why: The duration of one indexed subsegment, in the timescale of the enclosing sidx; it is timing data derived from the media the generator wrote and any uint32 is legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Uniform durations let a reader compute any subsegment's start time by multiplication; varying durations force it to accumulate the reference table; zero means a degenerate reference that a reader must handle specially.

diversity_axes.why: The trun per-sample duration, present only when its flag bit is set; it is derived from the media and is a free uint32, and its absence is equally legal because tfhd or the next trun supplies the value.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A constant duration gives constant-frame-rate fragments; varying durations give variable-frame-rate material; an omitted duration makes a reader fall back to default_sample_duration in tfhd or trex, which is a different lookup path.

diversity_axes.why: The trun per-sample presentation offset; at version 0 it is an unsigned uint32 and at version 1 a signed int32, so both the value and the sign capability are free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means decode order equals presentation order and a reader skips the reordering buffer entirely; non-zero makes it hold and reorder samples; negative values (version 1 only) reach the signed-offset arithmetic that version 0 cannot express at all.

diversity_axes.why: The tfhd and trex fallback sample duration; it is free uint32 data whose presence is itself flag-gated, so both the value and whether the field exists are open choices.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Present with no per-sample trun durations means every sample inherits it, taking the constant-duration path; absent means the reader falls back to trex; a zero value makes the fragment declare no timing at all, which reaches the unknown-duration handling.

diversity_axes.why: The presentation time of the first referenced subsegment in sidx; it is a uint32 at version 0 and a uint64 at version 1, and any value is legal because it anchors the index rather than describing the media.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero anchors the index at the start of the presentation and takes the simple path; a large value makes a reader offset every subsegment time, and only version 1 can express values above 2^32, which reaches the wide-time arithmetic.

diversity_axes.why: The mehd declared total duration of the fragmented presentation; it is a uint32 at version 0 and a uint64 at version 1, and it is free because the box is optional and only advisory.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Absent (no mehd at all) makes a reader discover the length by scanning fragments; present and exact lets it allocate the timeline up front; present but larger or smaller than the real total reaches the mismatch handling; zero means an unknown or live duration.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd time at which the movie preview begins; QuickTime presentation metadata with no effect on the media and no legal-value restriction.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means no preview and skips the whole preview path; a non-zero value makes a QuickTime-aware reader validate it against the movie duration and, if in range, expose preview-start metadata, which is a distinct branch from the normal playback setup.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd length of the preview; free metadata in movie timescale units.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero disables the preview; a duration longer than the remaining movie reaches the clamp path; a normal value makes a reader expose a preview range, which is code that ordinary playback never enters.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd time of the poster frame; free QuickTime metadata.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means no poster frame and skips the still-image extraction path; a value in range makes a reader seek to that timestamp and decode one frame, exercising the single-frame seek path; an out-of-range value reaches the clamping or rejection handling.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd start time of the current movie selection; free QuickTime editing metadata that no decoder is required to honour.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means no stored selection and takes the default full-movie path; a non-zero value makes a QuickTime-aware reader set an initial selection range, which reaches the range-clamping code and interacts with selection_duration.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd length of the stored selection; free metadata whose legal values include zero and anything up to the movie duration.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means an empty selection; a duration covering the whole movie is equivalent to no selection but reaches different validation; a partial duration makes a reader restrict playback and expose a subrange.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd stored playback position; free metadata that is meaningful only as a hint and has no structural role.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means start at the beginning and skips the resume path; a non-zero in-range value makes a reader seek before the first frame is decoded, reaching the resume-and-seek code; an out-of-range value reaches the clamping path.

diversity_axes.why: The creation timestamp of the movie, track or media as seconds since the 1904 epoch; pure metadata whose legal range spans more than a century and whose width is version-selected.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the conventional 'unknown' value and skips conversion; a 1904-epoch value, a modern UTC value and a value above 2^32 (version 1 only) each reach different time-conversion arithmetic, and only the large values exercise the 64-bit path.

diversity_axes.why: The modification timestamp, the counterpart of create_time and free for exactly the same reasons, including that it need not be greater than or equal to create_time.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero, equal to create_time, later than create_time and earlier than create_time each reach different metadata handling; a reader that computes an age or validates ordering exercises comparison code only when the two differ.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd preferred playback rate as an fp32 (16.16); free data whose canonical value is 1.0 but which the format does not restrict.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Unity takes the normal-speed path; other values make a player resample audio or drop and repeat video frames; zero reaches the paused-state handling; a negative value reaches the reverse-playback path that no positive value can.

diversity_axes.why: The mvhd preferred volume as an fp16 (8.8); free data, and values above unity are legal because the field is a hint rather than a limit.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Unity is the pass-through gain; zero mutes and may skip the audio path entirely; values above 1.0 reach the gain-amplification and clipping code; negative values reach the phase-inversion handling.

diversity_axes.why: The smhd audio balance as an fp16; free data spanning full-left to full-right and beyond, since the field is not range-checked by the format.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is centred and takes the equal-gain fast path; negative and positive values apply asymmetric gain to the two channels, reaching the stereo-panning arithmetic; out-of-range values reach the clamping path.

diversity_axes.why: The smhd or tkhd track volume as an fp16; free data and the per-track counterpart of preferred_volume.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Unity passes audio through unchanged; zero silences the track, which a mixer may optimise away entirely; other values apply a per-track gain and reach the mixing arithmetic that unity skips.

diversity_axes.why: The mdhd quality field, a free uint16 hint about rendering quality; the format assigns it no semantics beyond being present, so every value is legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the common default and skips quality handling; a non-zero value makes a QuickTime-aware reader expose it as a render-quality hint, and only distinct values across tracks make it a usable tie-breaker in track selection.

diversity_axes.why: The version of the protection scheme named by schm scheme_type; free uint32 data that refines which fields the scheme expects, and different schemes use different version spaces.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: For 'cenc' and 'cbc1' version 1 is the base layout while version 0x00020000 and above add the pattern fields (crypt_byte_block and skip_byte_block), so the value literally selects which following bytes exist; a reader that does not recognise the version takes the reject-or-ignore path.

diversity_axes.why: The constant initialisation vector shared by every sample of a track, used only by the 'cbcs'-family schemes; its length is set by default_constant_IV_size and its bytes are opaque key material, so both are free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: An 8-byte IV, a 16-byte IV and a zero-length IV each make the decryptor take a different IV-loading path, and a constant IV selects the per-track-IV code rather than the per-sample senc path, which is a structurally different decryption loop.

diversity_axes.why: The saio auxiliary-info-type parameter, present only when the flags bit is set; it is a free uint32 that further qualifies the auxiliary information type named beside it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the common case and takes the unqualified path; a non-zero value makes a reader match a specific parameterisation of the auxiliary type before it will use the offsets, and a mismatch makes it skip the auxiliary data entirely.

diversity_axes.why: The saiz auxiliary-info-type parameter, the saiz counterpart of the saio field and free for the same reasons; the two must agree for a reader to pair sizes with offsets.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Present only under the same flag bit; a value matching saio's lets a reader bind the size table to the offset table, while a differing value makes it look for another saiz/saio pair, reaching the multi-auxiliary-type search path.

diversity_axes.why: The hdlr component flags mask, a free uint32 that says which bits of the adjacent flags field are significant; it is metadata about metadata and the format does not restrict it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero means no flag bits are masked and a QuickTime-aware reader tests the raw flags; a non-zero mask makes it AND the flags first, reaching the masking arithmetic; masks that hide every bit make the handler-decision fall back to the FourCC alone.

diversity_axes.why: The hdlr component manufacturer FourCC; free data naming a vendor, with 'appl' and zero both common and every other FourCC legal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero takes the vendor-agnostic path; 'appl' makes a QuickTime-aware reader apply Apple-specific handler interpretation; an unrecognised vendor reaches the generic fall-through. Each is a distinct branch in the handler setup.

diversity_axes.why: The reserved gap in sidx, smhd, mvhd and tkhd, spelled once but declared with a different width in each branch; the format requires zero yet no reader validates it, so the bytes are free in practice.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the expected value and every reader skips the bytes without testing them; non-zero values are still accepted because the fields are never checked, so the choice cannot change decoder behaviour but does change the file's byte content and therefore any byte-level differ or hash.

diversity_axes.why: The reserved byte of the tenc payload; ISO/IEC 23001-7 requires zero, but a container parser reads it and moves on without testing it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Zero is the conforming value; a non-zero value is still parsed because the field is skipped, so it cannot alter the decryption path but does alter the bytes a DRM-aware reader stores and echoes back.

diversity_axes.why: A reserved byte of the tenc payload when version is 0, and a uint64 reserved field of tkhd at version 1 under the same spelling; in both cases the format requires zero and no reader validates it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Because the two branches share the identifier, the same key covers an 8-byte tkhd gap and a 1-byte tenc gap; neither is tested, so the value cannot change behaviour, but the width difference means the bytes occupy different amounts of the box in each case.

diversity_axes.why: The uint16 reserved gap between volume and matrix_structure in tkhd; required zero by ISO/IEC 14496-12 and never validated by a reader.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Read purely to keep the field offsets aligned, so any value yields a fully processed track header; leaving it free adds two unconstrained bytes per track without risking depth.

diversity_axes.why: The two high bytes of the 24-bit tkhd flags word; reserved by both QTFF and ISO/IEC 14496-12 and masked off by every reader, so the bytes carry no meaning and cannot reduce diversity if left free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Readers AND the flags word with 0xF (or 0xF and the version) before testing any bit, so no value in these two bytes can reach a different branch; they are free bytes that change the file's content without changing its interpretation.

diversity_axes.why: The four reserved bits above the four track flag bits in the tkhd flags low byte; masked away before any flag test, so they are free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Because a reader masks the low byte with 0xF, bits 7-4 are unreachable as control flow; leaving them free costs no depth and adds unconstrained bits per track.

diversity_axes.why: The two high bytes of the 24-bit vmhd flags word; reserved and never validated.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Only the single no_lean_ahead bit of vmhd flags is defined, and readers mask the rest, so no value here changes behaviour; the bytes are free.

diversity_axes.why: The seven reserved bits of the vmhd flags low byte, sitting above no_lean_ahead; masked away and never validated.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Unreachable as control flow for the same masking reason, so any value is safe and the bit is free to vary.

diversity_axes.why: The content region of any box the template routes through its default FSkip branch: free, skip, wide, mdat, meta, and every codec configuration child. Its byte length is whatever boxheader.size says, and its contents are unconstrained except where another entry imposes a payload requirement on that specific box type.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: For padding boxes the bytes are skipped without being read, so their content is irrelevant and their length is the only thing that matters; for mdat and the sample-entry children the same field is governed by the payload_wellformedness entries, which derive the bytes from the tables rather than the other way round.
